name: Black Horse
description: Black Horse (now called Cappall Dubh) is a pub in Aldgate, London, open every day from 11am to 1am. The page highlights its fresh energy at the same location and points visitors to an Events page for a full lineup. It also mentions functions and parties, with space for birthdays, work dos and other gatherings. The venue is described as having sports on TV, a dartboard, and great music, with examples of ticketed events listed in the “Upcoming Events” section.

name: Commercial Tavern
description: Commercial Tavern is a Victorian corner pub in Spitalfields (142–144 Commercial Street, London E1 6NU) with large windows and eccentric decoration. It features an upstairs cocktail bar with velvet booths and curated playlists. The venue focuses on rotating craft beers, expertly mixed cocktails, and a burger offering from Meat Stop, described as dry-aged British beef with house-made sauces. The page also highlights “Games” and a “hidden Fitzrovia favourite” vibe for the cocktail bar, making it suitable for dates and discreet meetups.

name: Duke of Somerset
description: Duke Of Somerset London is a city pub with decadent decor and a large external beer garden. It offers a great range of craft beers and premium spirits, including an extensive gin range, plus a cocktail menu. The venue is well set up for sport viewing, with 14 internal TVs and external viewing, and it lists Sky Sports and TNT Sports with HD screens. Facilities include Wi‑Fi and accessible toilets, and there’s a dartboard. Live music is listed, and children are welcome with a family policy of no children after 7pm on Thursday and Friday nights.

name: Duke of Wellington
description: The Duke of Wellington at 12 Toynbee Street (E17NE) is promoting “game nights” and big-screen football viewing. The page highlights FIFA World Cup fixtures and encourages visitors to come with a pint for non-stop football action. There’s also a booking contact email shown for booking inquiries.

name: Goodman's Field
description: The Goodman’s Field is a Wetherspoon pub in 87–91 Mansell Street, Tower Hamlets, London. It’s open daily from 8:00am until 11:00pm, with children under 18 only allowed on the premises between 8:00am and 10:00pm. Facilities include Wi‑Fi, TV screens and a licensed outside deck area, plus step-free access. The pub offers children’s meals (including pizzas) for £4.99 and £5.75, served with a drink and fruit. The page also includes a detailed local history of the surrounding land and mentions guest ale and craft tasting notes, along with a range of spritz cocktails.

name: Grapeshots
description: Grapeshots is a popular local wine bar tucked away down a narrow Victorian passage near Liverpool Street. It has a warm, cosy atmosphere with wood panelling and candlelit tables, plus antique curiosities and historic wine artefacts collected over decades. Guests can enjoy a diverse wine list and an interesting selection of craft beers, alongside modern British cooking on the food menu using seasonal ingredients that are UK and, where possible, locally sourced. The downstairs dining area suits group dining and drinks parties, and the venue can be hired for private events. It also hosts wine tastings and live music as part of its upcoming events.

name: Kings Stores
description: The Kings Stores is a vibrant, “hidden gem” pub in Whitechapel, nestled between the City and Spitalfields market. It has a diverse crowd and offers a lively World Cup atmosphere, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports. The venue serves a la carte dining and pub classics such as fish and chips, plus small plates and sharing dishes. There are private rooms for parties, meetings and get-togethers, each with its own private bar. Facilities include disabled access, family friendly features, WiFi, and functions. The page also promotes a Spring–Summer menu and Friday Prosecco offers.

name: Knave of Clubs
description: The Knave of Clubs is a historic East End pub on the corner of Bethnal Green Road and Club Row, brought back to life after being closed for 30 years. It’s open daily and serves Guinness alongside oysters and rotisserie chicken, with food available all day. The pub offers beers, wine and cocktails, and reservations are available online with walk-ins welcome. The venue also features One Club Row above the pub, inspired by New York taverns and Paris bistros, with long lunches, late dinners, dining at the bar, people watching, and two private dining rooms for parties.

name: Leman Street Tavern
description: Leman Street Tavern is a pub in Aldgate, described as “Aldgate’s shining gem” where the City of London meets the East End. It offers a heated, covered beer garden and a range of spaces for dining, drinks, and celebrations, including a fully private room called “The Chambers” and an outdoor terrace. Food is a key focus, with “Best of British Classics,” seasonal menus, and “Legendary Sundays” featuring Sunday roasts and double-egg Yorkshire puddings. The venue also promotes World Cup 2026 viewing “across our screens,” with big-match atmosphere. Food is served from 12:00–21:00 on Sundays, and the pub is open Sunday 12:00–22:00.

name: London Hospital Tavern
description: The London Hospital Tavern (LHT) was built for the builders of the hospital that shares its name, over 150 years ago, as a place to enjoy a pint after work. Today it continues that tradition for NHS staff and the local community. The pub offers food via a menu you can check before you arrive, alongside a wide selection of beer, wines and spirits, including a cocktail of the month and constantly rotating ales. There’s also a house bottled beer with 10p from every bottle sold going to the Air Ambulance Charity. Upstairs, the Mosaic bar hosts midweek live entertainment such as comedy, storytelling, improv and jazz, with more event nights at weekends.

name: Ninety One
description: Ninety One is a modern pub on Brick Lane, set within the Old Brewmaster's House of the Truman Brewery. It’s described as a cosy neighbourhood hangout with a warm, laid-back atmosphere. The venue is set up for dining alongside quality live music, which then flows into signature DJ nights that run late, with the dance floor coming alive on weekends. Food is available via a dedicated Food Menu and a Sunday roast menu. Opening times are listed for Wednesday through Sunday.

name: Pride of Spitalfields
description: The Pride of Spitalfields London is an authentic East End pub just off Brick Lane, offering traditional vibes and a warm, inviting atmosphere. The page highlights an exceptional beer selection with cask ales and well-kept pints, including a cracking Guinness at notably reasonable prices. Inside, it’s described as cozy and unpretentious, with worn carpets, comfy seats, and a roaring fire, creating a classic “public house” feel. There’s also mention of a lively standing crowd and an outside patio/street area that can be packed on sunny days. The venue is presented as a community hub with piano nights mentioned as a regular feature.

name: Princess Of Prussia
description: The Princess of Prussia is a traditional, historic pub in Whitechapel, close to Tower Bridge and the Tower of London. Inside, it features original ornate ceramic mouldings, cornices and fascia tiles, with a cosy traditional bar serving real ales from Shepherd Neame. It offers lunchtime food with a Thai twist (including Jungle Curry and Drunken Noodles) plus fish and chips, available 12–3pm daily. There’s also an alfresco experience in a secret, covered and heated beer garden, where food and drink are served up to 10pm.

name: The Astronomer
description: The Astronomer is a pub in one of London’s most vibrant areas, drawing style inspiration from the night sky and offering a lively atmosphere. It serves fresh, well-kept cask ales, craft beers and cocktails, alongside a dining menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients. The Rocket Room downstairs can cater for private events including business meetings, weddings and birthdays. The venue also highlights board games, free WiFi and accessibility features, and it welcomes families and assistance dogs. Food is served daily with set food serving times.

name: The Bell
description: The Bell is an independently owned Victorian pub on the fringes of the City on Middlesex Street, near Petticoat Lane Market and Jack the Ripper territory. It’s easy to reach from Liverpool Street and Aldgate underground stations, and is known for a mixed crowd of local residents and office workers. The pub is eclectically decorated and features two function rooms, including a games room with a pool table, darts and table football, plus an upstairs function room for rehearsals, meetings, performances and screenings. There’s also street art updates. Food is available via Detroit Pizza delivery or by bringing food from the local market, alongside craft beer on tap and in fridges.

name: The Blind Beggar
description: The Blind Beggar is a “wet-led” pub in Whitechapel, London, known for its regularly updated beer lineup and wide range of beer styles, from lagers to craft ales. The pub has a long history, including being the former brewery tap of the Manns Albion brewery and being built in 1894 on an earlier inn site. It’s also noted for its famous cultural connections, and hosts events such as “The Krays: Ronnie, Reggie and Me” with Fred Dinenage. The venue features an award-winning beer garden with a decked pergola, heated outside bar, and comfortable seating.

name: The Brown Bear
description: Nestled at 139 Leman Street in the vibrant Whitechapel district of London, the Brown Bear stands as one of the East End's most storied public houses. This Grade II listed Victorian gem, with its striking blue facade and bear motifs, has served as a social anchor for over two centuries. Its history mirrors the area's transformation—from 18th-century industrial bustle to the gritty underbelly of Victorian London, through wartime resilience and into the multicultural hub it is today.

name: The Buxton
description: The Buxton is described as a small wine bar and hotel with big character at the foot of Brick Lane in London. The site highlights an “Eat & Drink” offering with a bar menu curated with working relationships with brewers and winemakers. It also offers accommodation: 15 simple, paired-back bedrooms for the modern traveller, with room booking and an email contact for queries. The page notes the venue is open now and provides opening hours (7AM to 11PM).

name: The Crown and Shuttle
description: The Crown and Shuttle is an old-school East-End boozer on Shoreditch High Street in East London. The venue offers food via a “Daily Menu” and has drink menus, with opening hours that vary by day and can change for events and sports matches. It’s set up for groups, with table areas for drinks and private spaces for parties. The pub also hosts entertainment upstairs at Filthy Fanny’s, including weekly life drawing classes, life music, comedians, and other “louche entertainment”. There are references to a beer garden, and the site highlights seasonal events and match-related viewing.

name: The George Tavern
description: The George Tavern is a legendary public house in London’s east end, known for its thriving artistic community. Owner Pauline Forster has spent the last decade turning The George into an arts, music and performance venue with an international reputation. The pub offers live music from a range of artists, alongside the comfort of a classic East-End boozer. It also serves fresh hand-stretched pizza in the garden, with the kitchen open Wednesday to Sunday from 6pm til late. The venue includes a cosy dining area at the back of a patio and has a distinctive “Save The George” design associated with London’s indie-music scene.

name: The Gun
description: The Gun in Spitalfields is an East London community hub by Spitalfields Market, described as an “East London favourite since the 17th Century”. It offers a craft drinks selection alongside seasonally rotating menus inspired by British produce, including sharing plates and a noted Sunday roast. The venue also runs events such as Sunday roasts, cocktail masterclasses, and DJ nights (Thursday to Saturday). It has kitchen times listed and serves food daily with Sunday kitchen hours ending earlier. For sports fans, it mentions “big screens” and “every kick live” for World Cup match nights.

name: The Half Moon
description: The Half Moon is a pub at 213–223 Mile End Road, Mile End (Tower Hamlets). The building began as a former Methodist chapel built in 1900, later taken over by the Half Moon Theatre Company in 1977, and eventually converted into The Half Moon several years after the theatre closed in 1990. The venue offers Wi‑Fi, TV screens, and a licensed outside deck, with step-free access and baby changing facilities. Opening times run from 8:00am to late most days, with children under 18 only allowed on the premises between 8:00am and 9:00pm. Food and drinks can be ordered via the Wetherspoon app.

name: The Horn of Plenty
description: The Horn of Plenty is a small neighbourhood pub in the heart of Stepney Green, about 100 yards from the station. It’s described as intimate and cosy, with a huge selection of East End produce and local breweries, wines and spirits. The pub has 2 big screens/projectors showing football, rugby and other sporting events, plus a weekly quiz (Tuesdays) and themed quiz nights monthly. There are also NHS & student discounts on Wednesdays, a few boardgames, and a “cracking playlist”. Opening hours are listed for each day, and reservations are mentioned.

name: The Light Bar
description: The Light Bar is an independent bar and dining venue set in an old Victorian power station built in 1893, in Shoreditch, London. It spans three floors and is described as a modern bar and restaurant with “good times.” The page highlights new menus, later hours, and offers events such as bottomless brunch with world-class DJs, a Friday happy hour (2-4-1 cocktails between 4pm–8pm), and DJ nights every Friday and Saturday.

name: The Oliver Conquest
description: The Oliver Conquest dates from the mid 19th century and was originally called The Garrick, attached to the first Garrick Theatre behind the pub. The venue highlights a strong gin focus, with a current range of over 120 different bottles and new varieties added daily. There are featured gin and spirit selections including Japanese Gin with botanicals such as yuzu and juniper, spiced rum from the Sairen range, and a Black & Gold 11yo bourbon. The page also promotes booking a table and ordering via the site locator.

name: The Owl & the Pussycat
description: The Owl & the Pussycat is a popular Shoreditch pub on Redchurch Street, described as the “soul of Shoreditch” with an old-skool heart. It offers a food menu of hearty pub favourites, sharing boards and nibbly bits, plus beers on draft and seasonal cocktails. Sundays are a highlight, with epic Sunday roasts, bottomless Yorkies and unlimited gravy, plus a “Crumble Guy” mention. There’s an all-season, heated and covered beer garden at the rear, and the first-floor “Jago” space for food, drinks and cocktails. The pub also shows World Cup 2026 games live on big screens in proper pub style.

name: The Peacock
description: The Peacock is a traditional Irish pub in the back streets of East London, described as one of the last remaining original east end boozers in Stepney. Built in 1881, it survived WWII and was nicknamed “The Copper’s Pub” due to its location opposite the Thames Magistrate Court and Police Station. After redevelopment and refurbishment, it reopened in 2023 while keeping original features and character. The pub offers a menu of traditional Irish food (including stews and fish and chips mentioned) alongside a wide selection of drinks such as cask ales, craft beers, and over 20 Irish whiskeys. Live Irish music runs regularly, with live music every Friday and quiz night every Saturday.

name: The Running Horse
description: The Running Horse Aldgate is a bar in Aldgate, close to Aldgate East station, offering after-work pints, cocktails, and a food menu built around rotisserie cooking. Guests can enjoy craft beer from rotating taps and options like rotisserie chicken, smash burgers, and Sunday roasts (dry-aged beef rib, Cotswold white chicken, or Old Spot pork belly). The kitchen focuses on fire and flavour, including a 12-hour brine for free-range chicken. Sundays run 12pm–4pm, with a “Bottomless Roasts” offer including unlimited Prosecco and Bellinis for 90 minutes. The venue also supports group bookings with semi-private spaces and full venue hire, plus match-day viewing for major tournaments.

name: the Shoreditch Arms
description: The Shoreditch Arms is a lively pub in the heart of Shoreditch, serving food alongside craft beers, wines and spirits. During the week it offers lunch options and small plates, with a menu that includes classic pub food and cocktails. The venue also promotes “Bar Kick” in the basement as a gameday experience for live sport and sporting-and-gaming good times. There’s a hidden secret cocktail bar upstairs with velvet booths and curated playlists, described as a plush, low-lit escape. The page also highlights games and a private hire setup with an outdoor area and screens.

name: The Star by Liverpool Street
description: The Star by Liverpool Street is a karaoke-focused venue near Liverpool Street Station, with five private karaoke booths/rooms and themed spaces designed for singing into the early hours. It also offers two function rooms and a karaoke bar, plus regular karaoke nights, open karaoke, and events like Pub Quiz and 80s Musical Bingo Bottomless Brunch. Food is available via the dedicated Firestarter restaurant, with bar food including speciality burgers and sliders, sides and small plates using smoky, coal-roasted cooking techniques. The venue also highlights “two floors of the best live sports action”.

name: The Ten Bells
description: The Ten Bells is a historic East End London beer-factory pub in Spitalfields, described as a bustling, candle-lit social hub with a rock ’n’ roll twist. It serves an eclectic range of quality beers and an extensive cocktail menu, with a cocktail bar upstairs offering a curated selection of classics and Ten Bells signature cocktails. The venue is spread across three floors and is positioned as a great place to host events, just five minutes from Liverpool Street Station.

name: The White Hart
description: The White Hart, Whitechapel is a historic pub standing since 1750 and rebuilt around 1900, with a “second life” brought into the 21st century. It offers a relaxed, characterful atmosphere with craft beers (Hertfordshire brewed cask and keg), cocktails, popular wines and traditional British fayre, including a Sunday roast. Food is served alongside a range of menus (main, Sunday, kids, buffet) and allergen information. There’s an upstairs area used for a weekly quiz and private hire, plus outside tables for enjoying a pint while watching the world go by near Whitechapel station. The venue also runs events such as open mic night and quiz nights.

name: White Swan
description: The White Swan is a traditional pub in the heart of the City, described as a “hidden gem” in Aldgate East on the historic grounds of the old Half Moon Theatre. It serves a selection of Shepherd Neame beers, including rich seasonal ales, alongside an enviable wine list and an impressive spirits collection. The pub offers a welcoming atmosphere for relaxed evenings with friends or memorable meet-ups with colleagues. It also provides events and private hire, including a cosy function room for up to 25 guests and the option to hire the entire venue exclusively, with support for audio-visual equipment and whiteboards.

name: Williams Ale & Cider House
description: Williams Ale & Cider House is an East London pub in Whitechapel, tucked between the City and Spitalfields. It’s known for an extensive ale and cider collection, plus a delicious seasonal menu. The pub promotes a lively World Cup atmosphere and offers cask beer, including a guaranteed IPA and house bitter from national and local brewers. Food options range from bar snacks to burgers, and there are facilities including WiFi and a dog-friendly welcome. The venue also has darts, and it offers table booking and menu viewing online.

name: Coach and Horses
description: The Coach and Horses is an independent East London pub with roots since 1863 (and the current venue since 2018). It serves locally brewed beers, real ales, cocktails, Nepalese street food and Sunday roasts. The pub is family and dog-friendly, with a partially covered beer garden. There’s live music on Friday nights from 8pm, quiz nights, and live sport shown on six big screens indoors and outdoors—covering major football and rugby tournaments. It’s also a good spot for parties and whole-pub hire, with table bookings available.

name: King William IV
description: King William IV is an “East End original” pub, beautifully reborn under the stewardship of Walthamstow’s Exale Brewing. It pours 14 lines of tank-fresh beer and cask ale, plus cocktails and a curated wine list, in a laid-back, old-school setting. There’s a private events room and a beer garden, and the pub shows live sports for football, rugby and boxing nights. Food is available via Short Road Pizza, serving award-winning pizzas and Italian small plates. The venue also runs weekly deals and hosts events such as DJ nights, quiz nights, comedy and pottery classes. Kitchen hours are listed and children are welcome until 7pm.

name: Queer Brewing Project
description: Queer Brewing Project’s taproom in Leyton, East London, is on a peaceful industrial estate near Lea Bridge Station. It serves beer fresh from the brewery on 8 dedicated lines, alongside cans, cider, natural wine and snacks, with alcohol-free and gluten-free options available. The taproom welcomes dogs and children, is wheelchair accessible and step-free, and offers the option to order pizza to your table via local pizzeria Proud Mary. There are regular offers such as £5 pints from 4–6pm every Friday, plus events including a women’s Six Nations screening.

name: Heathcote & Star
description: Heathcote & Star is a lovingly restored pub in Leytonstone, described as having the biggest beer garden in the area. It offers an impressive drinks menu and food from The Dragon Flame, including BBQ dishes and Sunday roasts. The pub is positioned as a community spot for after-work drinks, with a games room and screens for live sport. It also hosts regular events such as pub quizzes, cocktail offers, and family film Fridays, alongside drink tastings, food nights, and beer pong tournaments. The venue offers private hire, including function rooms and booths, with options for conferencing and club nights.

name: Leytonstone Tavern
description: Leytonstone Tavern is an independent, community-focused neighbourhood pub and dining room in Leytonstone. It offers sustainably sourced, ethically reared produce alongside hand-picked craft beers and ciders. The venue is known for award-winning burgers, tacos and other street-food style dishes, with sample menus and regularly updated dishes. Kitchen hours run through the week with extended evening service. The pub also hosts events such as weddings, wakes, birthdays and BBQs, with an events team that creates bespoke experiences. There are also regular weekday offers like local pints, taco Tuesdays, wing Wednesdays and burger deals, plus takeaway beers.

name: Sir Alfred Hitchcock Hotel
description: The Sir Alfred Hitchcock Hotel in Leytonstone E11 offers a bar, restaurant and hotel, plus a venue for events. The “What’s On” section highlights regular food offerings such as Sunday Roast every Sunday (12:00 to 17:00), Thursday Steak Nights in the evening, and seasonal menus including a new menu from 17th January, a set Christmas menu from 20th November, kids menu, and a Christmas Day menu (25/12/25). Reservations can be made by calling 0208 530 3724, booking a room, or booking a table by email.

name: The Bell
description: Bell Leytonstone is a pub on 468 High Road, Leytonstone (London E11 3HN) with long opening hours. It’s positioned as a sports-focused venue, promising to show every match live and highlighting live tournament viewing such as World Cup 2026. The site also promotes “unbeatable drink offers” and mentions facilities including Wi‑Fi, HD screens, TNT Sports and Sky Sports. Live entertainment is also listed, alongside a newsletter sign-up for community news and updates.

name: The Birkbeck Tavern
description: The Birkbeck Tavern is a sports-focused pub with Sky Sports, BT Sport, Racing UK and At the Races, showing premiership and international football, rugby, cricket and golf. It also offers pool and darts, with free pool on Monday and Thursday. There’s a function room for birthdays, weddings, anniversaries and wakes, with a private bar and a separate garden area. The pub serves beer, wines and spirits, including a wide range of real ales and cocktails, plus wines and premium spirits. A hidden outdoor beer garden with seating is available all year, and BBQs are mentioned at weekends.

name: The Bull
description: The Bull is a friendly local pub in Wanstead (E11), just 100 yards from Wanstead Tube Station. It has a sunny beer garden “suntrap” with parasols, open every day until 11pm. The pub serves fresh, delicious food five days a week using locally sourced, sustainable ingredients, and it also offers a kids’ menu every day. Families are welcome, with “Little Bulls” welcome when accompanied by adults. Dogs are included too, with dog beds and bowls, dog snacks at the bar, and doggy roasts on Sundays (dogs kept on a lead).

name: The Cuckfield
description: The Cuckfield is an iconic London pub on Wanstead High Street, offering a memorable drinking and dining experience. It serves fresh, flavoursome home-cooked food alongside a diverse drinks menu. The page also highlights options such as a relaxed lunch, Sunday roast, family dinner and brunch, and provides online table booking and gift cards. Opening hours are listed for each day, and the address is 31 High Street, Wanstead (E11 2AA).

name: The Duke
description: The Duke is a Wanstead neighbourhood pub and dining room offering lunch and dinner, plus Sunday roasts and a rotating set of specials such as a Wednesday homemade pie and Thursday steak night. The site also highlights coffee from Perky Blenders and regular drink offers including a Monday club and a Mon/Tues burger deal. Entertainment features include DJ nights on Fridays and live music on the 1st Sunday of every month (DukeBox Sundays). The page also promotes events like neighbourhood social nights, happy hour, and themed occasions such as World Cup viewing and quizzes.

name: The George and Dragon
description: The George and Dragon in Wanstead offers a refined pub experience with expertly crafted British dishes, real ales, excellent wines and exciting cocktails. Enjoy the lively atmosphere in the bar or relax in the comfortable lounge, including a roast in Wanstead. The pub is known for classic pub food, juicy burgers and a Sunday roast, with dining options such as a cosy dining room. It also has big screens for live broadcasts of big matches, events and tournaments. When the sun is shining, there’s an inviting beer garden/terrace. It’s conveniently located near Wanstead Station and offers private spaces for parties and gatherings.

name: The Nightingale
description: The Nightingale on the Green is a historic East London pub in Wanstead, lovingly restored to keep the character of a traditional London pub while offering modern touches. It’s known for a wide selection of drinks, a modern kitchen, and catering for celebrations and special occasions. The pub has a function room called Madame Butterfield’s Lounge for events such as wakes, birthdays, christenings and more, with free WiFi for presentations. Football is a big theme: it claims to be the only local pub with Sky Sports and invites guests to watch live football in a lively atmosphere. There’s also a spacious beer garden for relaxing with a pint.

name: The Old Crown
description: The Old Crown is a community pub in the heart of Leytonstone, formerly known as “The Birds”. It’s positioned as a go-to spot for sport and big weekend entertainment, with pool tables and dart boards and a focus on cheering on favourite teams. The venue promotes regular events such as karaoke nights (every other Sunday) and live DJs every weekend, alongside community activities like life drawing sessions on Wednesdays. The pub also mentions a beer garden with £3 pints on draft, and frequent match-day viewing for football including Premier League and European competitions on screens.

name: The Red Lion
description: The Red Lion in Leytonstone has been part of the area since 1870, offering a welcoming pub atmosphere for locals and visitors. It serves seasonal British pub fare in both the restaurant and bar, with options for lunch, dinner and Sunday roasts. There’s seating in a newly refurbished garden/terrace, and the venue also has a stunning ballroom for regular events. For drinks, it pairs food with beers, fine wines and cocktails, including a secret cocktail bar upstairs. Guests can also stay overnight in characterful boutique hotel rooms above the pub.

name: The Rookwood Village
description: The Rookwood Village is a pub in Leytonstone (Cann Hall Road) for any occasion. It serves a wide range of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, including craft beers, wine and cocktails. Food is available with a fresh menu featuring pizzas, burgers, salads and sharers, plus fish and chips and stone-baked pizzas made on site. The venue has a private function room (“The Village Hall”) and a games-focused “Clubhouse” area with interactive darts, foosball, Ping Pong and more. It also promotes watching Sky Sports and TNT Sports on large screen TVs, and offers table bookings.

name: The Walnut Tree
description: The Walnut Tree is a JD Wetherspoon pub on 857–861 High Road, Leytonstone. It’s open early and closes late, with opening times listed daily. The pub has facilities including Wi‑Fi, TV screens, a licensed outside deck, meeting facilities, baby changing, and step-free access. The site also includes a “Pub history” section: the building is named after Walnut Tree House (later Essex Hall), a timber-framed structure dating from around c1500, with a walnut tree preserved in the garden when the property was leased in 1813. The page also references ordering food and drinks to your table via the Wetherspoon app, and mentions children’s meals and children’s menu content.

name: Toby Carvery
description: Toby Carvery Snaresbrook is a London carvery serving the “home of the roast” tradition for 40 years. The site highlights slow-roasted meats, fresh vegetables prepared every morning, and an all-you-can-eat carvery experience. Alongside the carvery, it offers vegetarian and vegan dishes, all-you-can-eat breakfast, and a children’s menu. The venue also has a range of beers, ciders, wines, spirits and hot drinks. Visitors can book a table online, and the page mentions inviting interiors, a spacious car park, baby changing facilities, and an inviting beer garden.

name: The Golden Fleece
description: The Golden Fleece in Manor Park is a community-focused pub with a historic feel and plenty to do. It serves pub food with specials such as sticky hoisin duck, sizzling pork belly, hot honey camembert and Sunday roasts. There’s a beer garden for outdoor drinks, plus family-friendly facilities and WiFi. Sports fans can watch live action with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and the venue hosts events like pub quiz nights (every Wednesday) and Six Nations and live football screenings. Amenities include a dartboard and outdoor play, and dogs are welcomed.

name: The Black Lion
description: The Black Lion Plaistow is a friendly local pub near Plaistow tube station, close to the Excel Exhibition Centre and within easy reach of Stratford and the London Stadium. Listed in CAMRA Good Beer Guide and Cask Marque, it offers real ales, premium beers, wines, spirits and specialist whiskies. The pub also has a menu of homemade pub food made from fresh, high-quality ingredients, with food served Mon to Fri (except bank holidays). There’s a large beer garden and free (patrons only) parking, plus a function room/stable bar available for birthdays, business functions and music events. The venue also shows a wide selection of sport on TV.

name: BrewDog
description: BrewDog Canary Wharf is in the heart of Canary Wharf at 2 Churchill Pl, London (E14 5RB). It’s open daily and offers stacked burgers, infamous wings and other bar food, with main and brunch menus available. The venue also has a lineup of fresh craft beer on tap, plus live sport shown on screens (Sky). There are offers such as Wings Wednesday (unlimited wings) and a lunch club deal, alongside events like beer schools and co-working “Desk Dog”. The page also notes dog-friendly status, vegan menu options, baby changing, and disabled access.

name: Pepper Street Tavern
description: Pepper Street Tavern is an independent pub in Canary Wharf, London, with a vibrant atmosphere and 20 rotating beer taps plus a range of wines, spirits and soft drinks. The gastro pub menu includes signature New York pizzas (12 or 20-inch) and hearty Sunday roasts, with chefs using quality locally sourced ingredients. Sports fans can watch major sporting events on 17 strategically placed high-definition screens. There’s also a games room with smart darts, a pool table, table tennis and retro arcade games, plus regular pub quizzes and live music nights. The venue offers spaces for corporate events, private parties and “work from the pub”, with TVs, projectors and charging points. Dogs are welcome.

name: Sports Bar & Grill

description: The Whitecross Tap London is a pub in Islington, just a few minutes’ walk from Old Street tube station. It’s a great spot for a relaxing drink, with 16 craft taps offering local beers and guest ales, plus a wide gin selection. The venue also serves pizzas (sourdough pizzas mentioned) and has Food Served hours. Facilities include TNT Sports and Sky Sports, with HD screens for watching sport. There’s an outside area and a beer garden, along with Wi‑Fi and a smoking area. The pub is dog friendly and has a family policy asking under-18s to leave by 6pm.

name: Two Brewers
description: The Two Brewers is a traditional, family-run London boozer with a warm, lively atmosphere and friendly service. It’s set at the start of the Whitecross Street food market, a short walk from the Barbican Centre, and offers a classic pub vibe. The pub has a dart board and focuses on drinks, with a range of lagers, four rating ales (including an ever-changing guest ale), fine wines, quality spirits, and soft drinks. Although it doesn’t serve food, you’re welcome to bring your own to enjoy with a proper pint.

name: Beechwood
description: Beechwood is Shoreditch’s premier sports bar, tucked between Liverpool Street Station and the heart of Shoreditch. It offers good food, great drinks and live sport, with a sprawling terrace, wall-to-wall HD screens and a vibrant match-day atmosphere. The venue screens major matches across football, Six Nations rugby, F1, tennis and NFL Sundays, with giant indoor and outdoor screens. Inside there’s a bright, open bar with comfortable seating, and a menu for different appetites, suitable for brunch or kick-off. There are also social activities such as shuffleboard and private areas for events and big-match screenings.

name: Finch's
description: Finch’s is a pub on Finsbury Square, just a short walk from Moorgate, Old Street and Liverpool Street stations. It’s set across two floors with private and semi-private areas, including Henry’s Den, a hidden gem for meetings, birthday celebrations, office parties and weddings. The venue has a quirky vintage feel, with London craft beers, a carefully selected wine list and local London spirits. Food is a key focus, with chef’s specials and British pub classics made with fresh seasonal ingredients, offering breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner. The pub also promotes big-screen World Cup 2026 match viewing.

name: Long Arm Pub & Brewery
description: Long Arm Brewery & Tap Room is a brewery and tap room serving tank-fresh craft beer brewed on-site and poured straight from tank to glass. The venue promotes unfiltered, additive-free beer with rotating seasonal selections including lagers, pale ales and stouts. It also highlights live sport with “two giant projectors” and other giant screens, covering football, rugby and more. The pub offers event spaces for occasions such as team lunches, birthday parties and corporate functions, with screen-and-sound technology for a sports-venue atmosphere. Bookings are available via the site.

name: Nancy Spains
description: Nancy Spain’s is an Irish pub brand with three lively locations across London and Manchester (Shoreditch, Monument and the Northern Quarter). The venue is described as “the home of Murphys”, serving Murphy’s Irish Stout and offering a warm, authentic Irish hospitality with a vibrant city-night-out atmosphere. It highlights live music every night and “lively trad performances seven nights a week”, with singalong tunes and a dancefloor. The site also promotes private hire for office parties and group gatherings, with spaces in each location.

name: The Flying Horse
description: The Flying Horse is an authentic British pub in Liverpool Street (Finsbury, London), a short walk from Liverpool Street and Moorgate stations. It serves pub classics with a strong drinks focus, including an excellent range of cask ales, lagers, wines, cocktails and a huge range of spirits. Food is available with day and night menus (11am–4pm and 4pm–9pm) and pizzas available all day, plus burgers, rustic pizzas and lunchtime sandwiches. The pub has several HD TV screens and a large screen projector for live sport, and it also offers an upstairs function room for private hire with TV screens, a private bar, and a dartboard.

name: The Fox
description: The Fox is a traditional East End corner pub in Shoreditch, lovingly restored with a modern twist. It’s known for a fantastic selection of world beers and London gins. Spread over three floors, it has a ground-floor bar, a first-floor function room with a second bar, an outdoor roof terrace, and a private Karaoke Den for up to 20 guests. The pub runs an Asian-inspired home-cooked food menu and also offers a Coop pop-up food residency. Live sport is shown, with all the big tournaments available to watch. Open Monday to Saturday, it’s a relaxed spot for drinks, food, and karaoke nights.

name: The Griffin
description: The Griffin is a cosy craft beer pub in Shoreditch (Old Street area), offering a wide range of craft beers on draught and in bottles, plus global wines and spirits. The venue is described as having warm dark-wood decor and nostalgic vintage features, with a nostalgic vintage bar. There’s also an upstairs secret cocktail bar with velvet booths, curated playlists and a cocktail menu including classics like the French Martini and Smoked Old Fashioned. The page also highlights “Beer Flight Sundays” and a games section, alongside options for bookings and private hire.

name: The Joiner on Worship
description: The Joiner on Worship in Shoreditch is a three-floor pub described as a “three-floor sanctuary” combining traditional Irish hospitality with a vibrant queer energy. It offers a relaxed visit for a quiet stout or a burger, plus a weekly live music sing-song. The venue also has games and fun features including free shuffleboard, a beer pong table, and a photo booth. There’s a huge upstairs function room with a private bar for corporate parties and private events. The name pays tribute to the craftsmanship of 1860, when the building began as a furniture warehouse for Moore and Hunton.

name: The Old Blue Last
description: The Old Blue Last is described as a “300 years of history” east-end boozer and live music venue, said to be haunted by Shakespeare. The page highlights a busy 7-day weekly programme and “live music sessions”, with events promoted via ticket links. It also advertises late-night weekends running from 11pm to 3am, plus specific dates such as “East London Block Party” on 25th July. Table booking is promoted for events, suggesting visitors can reserve in advance.

name: The Princess of Shoreditch
description: The Princess of Shoreditch is a historic pub in the heart of East London, with a storied history dating back to the early 19th century. It has grown from a modest tavern into a cherished Shoreditch landmark, and is one of four pubs within the Noble Inns group. The pub focuses on seasonal menus with British provenance, sourcing ingredients from local farmers, butchers, greengrocers and fishermen. Food options include a la carte dishes, a weekday set lunch menu, and a Sunday roast served until 8pm. The venue also offers private dining across both floors, including a first-floor private dining room and exclusive hire for larger parties.

name: The Windmill
description: The Windmill has been welcoming customers since 2006, combining a Traditional English Pub with Modern Italian Food. The owner, Alberto, describes how the concept built a strong food and drinking clientele, and how the pandemic led to introducing pizza—especially Roman-style pizza made with quality ingredients by a professional Italian pizza chef. The pub offers craft beers, cocktails, and a menu featuring Roman style pizza (including options like Rocket and Parma Ham, Napoletana, Calzone, Lasagna and Gnocchi), plus wines. There’s also a gallery to have a look around.

name: Dirty Dicks
description: Dirty Dicks is a City of London pub and dining room on Bishopsgate, close to Liverpool Street Station. With history dating back to the early 1800s and a “hearty welcome since 1745”, it’s split over two floors for lunch or dinner, then comes alive in the evening. The pub serves ales, premium wines and seasonal British food including homemade pies, fish & chips, and a traditional Sunday roast. There’s also an underground cocktail bar, WM Barker, and a subterranean private space called The Vaults. The venue has large TV screens for live FIFA World Cup 2026 matches and offers food and drink packages for matchdays.

name: Hamilton Hall
description: Hamilton Hall is a Wetherspoon pub located at Liverpool Street station, in the street-level concourse of the City of London. It’s open early to late (7:00am–11:30pm on weekdays, 9:00am–10:30pm on Sundays). The pub is named after Lord Claud Hamilton and is described as the former ballroom of the old Great Eastern Hotel. Facilities include Wi‑Fi, step-free access, and a licensed outside area (deck). The venue also promotes ordering food and drinks to your table via the Wetherspoon app, and has children’s meals available for £4.99.

name: Lord Aberconway
description: The Lord Aberconway is an historic pub with a “quirky vibe” in a traditional setting, located in Old Broad Street just a short walk from Liverpool Street Station. The pub is described as a purveyor of “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”, with tempting dishes on British pub classic menus. Visitors can book a table, order at the table, or walk in. The page also highlights loyalty and ale & gin trails, including a “Financial District” trail, and mentions nearby central London attractions such as the Gherkin, Guildhall, and Brick Lane.

name: Red Lion
description: The Red Lion Moorgate is a traditional Victorian pub dating back to 1887, tucked between Moorgate Station and Liverpool Street Station. It’s described as family-friendly and offers expertly brewed real ales in a warm, cosy setting. The pub also promotes “Delicious Pub Food”, including small plates and pub classics, with a dedicated Sunday Roast offering. Facilities listed include being dog friendly, WiFi, and offering functions. There are also references to big match viewing with “big screens at the ready” for World Cup bookings, and a “See What’s On” section for events.

name: The Botanist
description: The Botanist is located in the heart of Broadgate Circle, London. It’s described as more than a restaurant—your go-to spot for live music, weekend brunch, long lunches and late night drinks. The venue also has a basement bar called The Soda Room, which hosts Soda Sessions with live music on Wednesday and Thursday nights. Menus listed include à la carte, dessert, bottomless brunch, wine, drinks, and group dining/canapés, suggesting a full food and drink offering for both casual visits and groups.

name: The Globe
description: The Globe is a historic pub in Moorgate, London, described as a British pub with a 150+ year heritage. The venue is presented as a place for “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”, with British pub classic menus and dishes available to book a table, order at the table, or order for collection. It’s positioned in the heart of Moorgate, a short stroll from Moorgate and Liverpool Street Underground stations, with several central London attractions nearby. The page also references loyalty and ale & gin trails.

name: The Magpie
description: The Magpie is a historic pub in Devonshire Square, described as a traditional pub with a unique character. It’s known for an eclectic range of real ales and quality pub food served with “famous British hospitality”. The page highlights ways to book a table, order at table, and buy gift cards, and notes it’s located in Bishopsgate London within a short stroll of Liverpool Street Station, Bishopsgate and Houndsditch.

name: The Railway Tavern
description: The Railway Tavern (The Railway, London) is a family-friendly pub with foundations dating back to 1736. Originally called the Cow House, it was renamed after the invention of the railways in 1804. The pub offers pub food including breakfast, small plates and pub classics, plus a Sunday roast. It has a beer garden (weather permitting) and is set up for functions and venue hire. Sports fans can watch live football and rugby on Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with fixtures and big match promotions like the Six Nations. Facilities also include WiFi and darts (interactive darts, dartboard).

name: Woodin's Shades
description: The Woodins Shades is a historic pub in Bishopsgate, described as a traditional pub with unique character. It’s known for an eclectic range of real ales and quality pub food, served with “famous British hospitality.” The page highlights British pub classics including “unbeatable pies” and tempting dishes on British pub classic menus. Visitors can book a table, walk in, and also order at the table or for collection. The pub is positioned near Liverpool Street Station and other nearby transport links, making it a convenient stop in the City of London area.

name: Phoenix
description: The Phoenix is a modern City of London pub in Whitechapel, described as a welcoming local near Bank with a warm atmosphere and stylish touches. It offers fresh food and great drinks, with a Prix Fixe menu (two courses £18, three courses £22) and seasonal Spring/Summer menu. The pub promotes “World Cup” live moments and has Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with fixtures available to view. Facilities listed include WiFi and disabled facilities, and it’s dog friendly. There’s also venue hire for parties, birthdays, and meetings.

name: Goldwood
description: Goldwood is Bank Station’s “premier sports bar”, right in the heart of the City of London. With three bars across two floors, it’s built for after-work drinks, weekend watch-parties and late-night celebrations. The venue is known for wall-to-wall live sport shown in ultra-high-definition on screens in every direction, with unbeatable sound and an electric atmosphere. It also offers good food alongside cold pints, plus private spaces and flexible group packages for corporate socials and events. There’s a kids menu and a published food menu, and the site lists events such as Magic Breakfast and Shuffleboard.

name: Old Doctor Butler's Head
description: Old Doctor Butler’s Head is one of Moorgate’s oldest pubs, named after the court physician to King James I. The pub offers warm hospitality, rich history and a mix of traditional pub classics in the bar plus innovative, elegant restaurant cuisine using seasonal, well-sourced ingredients. It’s known for famously good cask ales and also has world wines and international lagers. Guests can sip in the traditional bar, dine in the restaurant, or enjoy an outdoor alfresco area in a bustling alley with olde-world charm. The venue also has live sport on TV with BT Sport and multiple screens showing football and more, and it offers function spaces for events and parties.

name: The Telegraph
description: The Telegraph in Moorgate is a Fuller's pub focused on quality food. It offers refined pub classics made from fresh, seasonal ingredients, with dishes freshly cooked in an open kitchen. The venue also supports private events, including business meetings, weddings and birthdays, with functions rooms available. The bar is well stocked with modern craft beers and cask classics. The page highlights accessibility features such as step-free access, baby changing facilities, families welcome, and assistance dogs welcome, plus comfy sofas and a covered smoking area.

name: The Tokenhouse
description: The Tokenhouse is a historic pub in Moorgate (4 Moorgate, London EC2R 6DA), described as London’s most convenient meeting place near seven tube stations. It offers refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, with food served on weekdays. The venue is set up for functions including business meetings, weddings, birthdays and private events. Guests can enjoy live sport with big screens showing TNT Sports fixtures and events, plus a well-stocked bar with craft beers and cask classics. Pub features include a pool table, darts board, free WiFi, air conditioning, families welcome, and assistance dogs welcome.

name: Aldgate Tap
description: The Aldgate Tap is housed in the striking Portsoken Pavilion. It serves coffee, a wide range of beers, wines and non-alcoholic drinks. The venue is also home to Ray’s Pizza, offering lunch and evening snacks.

name: The Alice
description: Alice Houndsditch London is a spacious, sophisticated bar near Aldgate station, offering a large gin selection (“Ginventory”) and a Meantime Tank with over 12 varieties of lagers and craft products. Food is available, including freshly baked pizzas and “feel-good dishes,” plus small plates for after-work drinks. The venue has facilities such as Wi‑Fi, accessible toilets, real ale, children welcome, HD screens, and baby changing. It also offers an outside area with a beer garden, smoking area, and Sky Sports and TNT Sports. Live entertainment is listed, and the pub can host parties of up to 500 guests.

name: The Craft Beer Co
description: The Craft Beer Co. St. Mary Axe is a City-centre pub with a large selection of beers, featuring 18 keg lines, 9 cask pumps, and 200+ bottles & cans. Alongside drinks, it offers a hearty selection of pies, scotch eggs and scratchings, with snacks available individually or as part of a sharing platter. The venue is positioned as a great spot for business meetings or after-work drinks, and it is available for private hire every weekend. The page also lists festive closure dates and provides contact details and opening hours.

name: The Lion Houndsditch
description: The Lion Houndsditch is a pub focused on drinks, offering a great selection of draught beers (including Guinness, Estrella, Peroni, and more) plus cocktails such as Maple Old Fashioned, Kraken Stormy, and Rhubarb Collins, along with house wine spritzers. The venue also caters for private hire on weekends, described as having a great atmosphere for parties with a twist on the traditional. The page encourages visitors to follow the pub on Facebook and Instagram for events and promotions.

name: The Old Tea Warehouse
description: The Old Tea Warehouse is a hidden City of London pub tucked down a historic alley near Aldgate. It offers craft beers, cocktails and seasonal food, with a private patio and an electronic darts room/downstairs darts club. The venue highlights interactive darts and WiFi, plus functions and disabled facilities. Food is served seasonally, with menu items mentioned such as scotch eggs and fish and chips. There are also darts-focused events like a “Darts Club”, and promotions such as £25 Prosecco bottles every Friday.

name: The Sterling Bar & Kitchen
description: The Sterling at the Gherkin is a City of London bar and restaurant on the ground floor of the Gherkin skyscraper. It’s described as offering spaces for after-work drinks, meetings, corporate events, wedding receptions, special occasions, and work lunches and dinners, as well as a bite to eat or drink with friends. The page also promotes watching the FIFA World Cup 2026 live, highlighting a matchday atmosphere with big screens and a cold pint. Opening hours are listed from 10am to 11pm (Mon–Wed) and 10am to 12am (Thu–Fri).

name: The Trinity Bell
description: The Trinity Bell is a City pub with vintage Victorian elegance. It offers a classic British lunch in its two-floor restaurant, alongside drinks and private events in the evening. The dining menu features refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients. The venue also supports private events such as business meetings, weddings, and other functions, with dedicated catering for different occasions. The pub lists features including families welcome, free WiFi, air conditioning, and assistance dogs welcome, and it serves food with published food serving times.

name: East India Arms
description: East India Arms is a historic London pub on Fenchurch Street, in the heart of the City. Serving traders and tourists since 1829, it was built in the latter part of the Georgian era, with the Magpie Ale House previously on the site from at least 1645. The pub offers a traditional setting with authentic wooden floors, classic furnishings, and old photos on the walls. It’s known for cask ales and lagers from Shepherd Neame, alongside a selection of wines, ciders, spirits, and soft drinks. The page also highlights an outdoor area and WiFi.

name: Hoop and Grapes
description: The Hoop and Grapes is a historic pub in Aldgate, described as one of central London’s oldest pubs. Built in 1593 and a Grade II listed building, it’s said to be the oldest licensed house in the city of London, with the Great Fire of London stopping just 50 yards away in 1666. The tall, slim building features sash windows, low ceilings and plenty of charm, and the front leans out after being twisted and bent by time. Originally named Hops and Grapes for selling beer and wine, it now offers a range of drinks including spirits and cocktails, alongside British pub classic menus with “unbeatable pies”.

name: The Chamberlain
description: The Chamberlain is a grand Edwardian hotel, premium pub and restaurant in Tower Hill. It offers a refined menu of pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, alongside a well-stocked bar with modern craft beers and cask classics. The venue is set up for dining, drinks, and private occasions, with functions rooms for business meetings, weddings and other events. Guests can also stay overnight, with accommodation and a 24-hour reception. Accessibility features include step-free access and an accessibility lift, and assistance dogs are welcome. Sports fans can enjoy big screen sports viewing.

name: The Cheshire Cheese
description: Cheshire Cheese London is a pub in the heart of London at 48 Crutched Friars, near the Tower of London and Tower Bridge. It’s positioned as a live sport venue, with 9 TVs and a big projector screen, plus Sky Sports and TNT Sports and HD screens. Food is served from 12:00–19:00, and there are menus to explore. The pub also offers real ale, darts (three dart boards), and a private upstairs bar for hire. It welcomes “your furry friends” and notes that children must leave by 9pm. Facilities listed include Wi‑Fi, accessible toilets, wheelchair access, and a pool table.

name: The Fenchurch
description: The Fenchurch is an independent pub operator’s venue, described as a proper pub run with care and passion. The team welcomes locals of all ages and preferences, with a warm, friendly atmosphere. Pete, who has worked in pubs since age 14 and trained with Mitchells & Butlers (Bass), is highlighted as the driving force behind creating and managing the pub in the City. The page mentions meticulous attention to details, including home-cooked food that is “absolutely delicious and generous,” alongside wines from an independent wholesaler. Social links are provided for events and promotions.

name: The Liberty Bounds
description: The Liberty Bounds is a Wetherspoon pub at 15 Trinity Square, Tower Hill in the City of London (EC3N 4AA). It’s open daily from 8:00am until midnight. Facilities listed include Wi‑Fi, TV screens, and step-free access. The page also mentions children’s meals priced at £4.99 and £5.75, served with a drink and fruit. The pub’s history notes it sits just outside the City of London’s “liberty” boundary and close to the site where prisoners from the Tower of London met their fate in the 16th and 17th centuries.

name: The Minories
description: The Minories London is a traditional pub near Tower Hill tube station, with easy walking access to attractions such as Tower Bridge and London Dungeon. It shows major sporting events on Sky and BT Sport across numerous plasma screens and two large projector screens, and it also has a heated beer garden with outdoor screens. The pub offers food served daily, alongside a wide selection of drinks including real ales and wines. Facilities include Wi‑Fi, HD screens, real ale, late licence, and a function area for private hire during the week, where packages can include food, drinks and DJs. Children are welcome.

name: Three Tuns
description: Three Tuns Aldgate is a friendly local pub in Aldgate, London (36 Jewry Street). It serves a range of delicious food and drink, with food served from 12:00 PM to 9:00 PM. The pub is set up for sports fans, advertising live sport with Sky Sports, TNT Sports, and HD screens, plus function and outside areas. Facilities listed include a beer garden, smoking area, real ale (Cask Marque approved), and a dartboard. It also notes Wi‑Fi and a dog-friendly pub link. The venue offers booking for tables and parties.

name: Balls Brothers
description: Balls Brothers Minster Court is a relaxed bar and restaurant with a classic vibe, offering a Modern British menu alongside fine wines and classic cocktails. It’s situated in the heart of the City just off Mincing Lane, making it a popular choice with the city crowd. The page also promotes watching the FIFA World Cup 2026 live, highlighting a matchday atmosphere, big screens, and a proper “cold pint” experience. Opening hours are listed for Monday to Tuesday (12pm–10pm), Wednesday to Friday (12pm–11pm), with Sunday and Saturday as private enquiries only.

name: BrewDog
description: BrewDog Tower Hill is a bar in the heart of the City at 21 Great Tower St, near Tower Hill Underground Station and a short walk from the Tower of London. The venue offers stacked burgers, infamous wings and bar food, plus a lineup of fresh craft beer on tap. It also highlights live sport on screens and shuffleboard for friendly competition. There’s a vegan menu, baby changing station, disabled access, and dog-friendly policy. The page also mentions a beer garden/outside tables area and provides main, brunch, and drinks menus, along with opening hours and regular offers/events such as Wings Wednesday and live sport (Sky).

name: Hung, Drawn and Quartered
description: The Hung, Drawn & Quartered is a historic Tower Hill pub near the Tower of London, serving freshly-prepared pub food and fine ales. It offers a new summer menu and a dining menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients. The venue also supports private events, including business meetings and celebrations such as weddings and birthdays, with functions rooms available. The bar is well stocked with modern craft beers and cask classics. Facilities include accessibility support (step-free access, baby changing, free WiFi) and families welcome. Dogs are explicitly welcomed, and assistance dogs are welcome.

name: Tank & Paddle Minster Court
description: Tank And Paddle Minster is a lively London venue near landmarks including the Tower of London, London Bridge and the Bank of England. It’s dog-friendly and serves delicious food on-site. The venue offers games such as shuffleboard and a dartboard, plus facilities including HD screens, Wi‑Fi and accessible toilets. It also lists Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with Sky TV and other TV options for watching sport. There are options for private hire and secondary rooms for events and occasions, making it suitable for group bookings.

name: The Hydrant
description: The Hydrant is Central London’s destination for dinner and drinks, described as a hive of activity. It hosts regular beer tasting sessions and mixology classes, with a craft-beer and real-ale bar plus seasonal cocktails. The dining offer includes a menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, and there are food serving times listed. The venue also supports private events, meetings and functions rooms, and has features such as step-free access, air conditioning, baby changing facilities, families welcome, free WiFi and comfy sofas. Accessibility and assistance dogs are mentioned, and the pub is located at Equitable House on Monument Street.

name: The Monument
description: The Monument is a contemporary, family-friendly corner pub in Whitechapel, opposite the monument to the Great Fire of London and near London Bridge. It offers a beer garden (weather permitting) and a welcoming indoor space with TVs on the walls. Food is a key part of the venue, with a menu worth discovering, deals, and highlights such as Sunday roasts and small plates to pub classics. The pub also promotes live sports viewing, including Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with fixtures and events like Six Nations and live football. Facilities listed include WiFi, disabled facilities, and dog-friendly access.

name: The Ship
description: The Ship (EST. 1802) is a pub in London’s Square Mile at 3 Hart Street. Inside, it’s known for a ceiling decorated with sailor hats, a friendly team, and a wide range of drinks including keg beers, cask ales, Guinness, spirits, and a diverse wine list. It’s open Monday to Friday for city workers, tourists and everyone in between, with weekends closed except for private hire. The page also highlights “What’s On?” with nights/events and a Top Deck booking option.

name: The Walrus & The Carpenter
description: The Walrus and The Carpenter is a historic pub in Monument, London, described as a British brand venue focused on “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”. The page promotes British pub classic menus with tempting dishes, and offers ways to book a table or order at table/for collection. It also highlights the pub’s location in the heart of the city, with nearby landmarks such as London Bridge, Tower Bridge, Borough Market, The Shard, and the Tower of London.

name: The Windsor
description: Windsor Fenchurch is a traditional pub in the heart of the city, next door to Fenchurch Street station. It’s known for live sport, with Sky Sports and BT Sports plus HD screens, and is described as being close to Tower of London and Tower Bridge. The pub serves a traditional food menu, with fish and chips highlighted as the top seller, alongside 5 cask ales, wines, craft bottled beer and ale, and a wide range of spirits. Facilities and features mentioned include a beer garden/outside area, Wi‑Fi, children welcome when eating, and a late licence.

name: Cock and Woolpack
description: The Cock & Woolpack is a small, friendly and unpretentious historic pub tucked away down a quiet street in the heart of the City of London, behind the Royal Exchange on Finch Lane. It’s described as “a local in the city”, offering a warm welcome and prompt, cheery service. The pub is positioned as a great central spot for a lunchtime drink with friends, with a range of craft beers and excellent cask ales, lagers and wines. It’s just minutes from Bank tube station, Leadenhall Market, The Bank of England and Liverpool Street.

name: Forge
description: Forge is a venue in Holborn suited to corporate lunches, get-togethers and after-work drinks. The site promotes “lunch and a drink” from £12.50 and a midweek dinner from a main menu. It also highlights facilities and features including a cocktail menu, food served, a function area, Wi‑Fi, late license, smoking area, accessible toilet, and live music. The page encourages visitors to book a table online to avoid disappointment.

name: George and Vulture
description: The George & Vulture is described as a City institution and a Chop House restaurant, known for its best chops and steaks. Alongside the restaurant, it is also open for drinks and cold platters in the evening. The page includes links to menus and dining/restaurant & private dining areas, suggesting spaces for dining and private functions.

name: Golden Goose
description: The Golden Goose is a walk-in venue located at 13–15 Leadenhall Market, London (EC1V 3LR). The page welcomes visitors and provides contact details via email. It also invites people to get in touch about working with the venue, including sending a CV to the provided email address.

name: Lamb Tavern
description: The Lamb Tavern is a traditional British pub in the heart of London, located in iconic Leadenhall Market. It’s an historic public house dating back as far as 1780, with three floors and an epic basement bar called Old Tom’s set within the arches beneath the market. The pub serves quintessentially British food inspired by the market’s heritage of meat, poultry and game, including bar snacks and hearty lunches, plus a wide selection of beers, ales, cocktails and wines. It’s positioned as a great spot for lunch and dinner, and the venue promotes big-match World Cup 2026 viewing across screens.

name: Pitcher and Piano
description: Pitcher & Piano in Cornhill is a quirky bar with cosy booths and tables by the bar, offering everything from bottomless brunches and leisurely lunches to after-work drinks. The venue is described as a place to stay all day, moving from morning coffee to midnight cocktails, with an all-day food menu including flatbreads, sandwiches, salads, burgers and small plates. Facilities listed include accessible access, high chairs, free WiFi and indoor screens. The page also highlights weekly deals such as a pint of Amstel offer and bottomless brunch bookings.

name: Simpson's Tavern
description: Simpson’s Tavern is described as “the oldest chophouse in London” and a historic London institution with heritage dating back to 1757. The venue is located at 38½ Cornhill. It highlights a restaurant/food offering and is well known for traditional English dishes, including stewed cheese and pork belly crackling. The page also notes the tavern was frequented by Charles Dickens and Samuel Pepys, giving it a strong literary and historical connection.

name: The Counting House
description: The Counting House is a beautiful pub and hotel in the City of London (EC3), celebrating 19th Century decadence. name: The Old Farmhouse

name: The Pineapple

name: The Rose & Crown

name: The Vine

name: Carlton Tavern

Guests access the hotel via a separate entrance through a historic cobbled courtyard into a secret patio area. The page highlights a private planted courtyard/patio and “super snug” and other cosy guest rooms, described as comfortable and intimate for solo travellers or couples. The location is described as a quiet residential area with gardens, cafés, and canals, with good transport links to London’s attractions.

name: Coopers Arms

The venue highlights a beer garden, HD screens, and Sky Sports and TNT Sports, suggesting it’s a good spot to watch sport. Opening times are shown for each day, with the pub open today from 11:00 AM to 10:00 PM.

name: Kilburn Bridge

name: North London Tavern
description: The North London Tavern is a family-friendly Victorian pub in Kilburn, built in 1894 for railway workers and still featuring original features such as ornate coving, original wooden floors and cast iron fireplaces. It offers a “menu worth discovering” with pub classics and small plates, including a Sunday Roast. The venue is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it shows live football and rugby (including Six Nations). There’s also a dartboard, WiFi, takeaway, and it’s dog friendly. The pub hosts events like the “Untapped - Battle of the Bands” and a pub quiz every Sunday.

name: Queens Arms

It offers premium cask and craft products, a good variety of wines, and a delicious food menu with downloadable lunch deals and main menu. The pub also has a large bar, sports bar/snug, and a restaurant that can be hired as a private function room. It’s described as a great entertainment hub, showing all major sporting events with SKY and BT, and featuring live music on Friday nights.

name: Sir Colin Campbell

It prides itself on Irish hospitality with a contemporary outlook, and describes itself as an LGBTQI+ friendly, inclusive and safe space. A standout feature is live traditional Irish music every Saturday and Sunday evening. The pub also shows major sporting fixtures on Sky Sports and TNT on two big screens, and hosts events including a weekly pub quiz. Food includes Pieminister pies (with sides and desserts) and a pizza menu for snacking.

name: The Alice House
description: Alice House is a comfortable, lively neighbourhood social with relaxed work-spaces by day and a social bar atmosphere by night. It offers fair trade coffee and seasonal food, including weekday lunches, Saturday brunch and Sunday roasts, alongside sustainably sourced food. In the evenings it serves independent local beers and wine, plus seasonal cocktails. The venue is described as a place to meet friends, enjoy an evening meal, or host an event where everyone is made to feel welcome. The page lists two London locations: West Hampstead and Queen’s Park, with bar and kitchen hours and phone contacts for each.

name: The Alliance

The menu changes regularly and includes “Alliance classics.” The pub also runs themed nights such as trivia, gaming and other events, creating a vibrant atmosphere for regulars in West Hampstead.

name: The Black Lion
description: The Black Lion in West Hampstead is a lively pub known for “feel-good” pub food, legendary cocktails and craft beer. The venue also runs regular events such as Rockeoke (karaoke with a live band) and “LIVE AT THE LION” with epic live bands on Friday and Saturday nights. It’s also set up for live sport, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and provides facilities like WiFi, disabled facilities, and family-friendly options.

name: The Black Lion

It’s an iconic Grade 2* listed pub and dining room opposite the Kiln theatre and a short walk from Brondesbury overground and Kilburn tube stations. The venue offers real ales, ciders, an eclectic wine list and beers on tap from around the world. Food is described as not standard pub fare, with vegetarian and vegan dishes plus meat, fish and bread from charcoal ovens, including dishes influenced by north Indian cuisine. There’s a bar snack and lunch menu, and a full menu in the dining room.

name: The Old Bell

The venue is known for showing live sport on multiple full-HD TVs, including Sky, BT Sport and Premier Sport, and it has plenty of TV screens. There’s a large beer garden/outside area for relaxing in summer, plus regular karaoke sessions and quiz nights. The pub also lists live music/live entertainment, real ale, cocktails, and facilities such as accessible and wheelchair access, late licence, and children welcome.

name: The Priory Tavern

The kitchen team serves award-winning food six days a week, including must-try Sunday roasts, plus children’s menus. The pub is located behind Kilburn High Road Overground, a short walk from Kilburn Park Tube Station, with street parking at weekends.

name: The Railway

Facilities include WiFi, disabled facilities, and a dartboard, and it’s described as dog friendly and family friendly. Booking a table is encouraged for drinks, food and events.

name: The Salusbury

The venue also has a private dining room for up to 14 guests. What’s on includes a monthly pub quiz and live music every Sunday evening (with “Single Deck Sundays” record sessions between 4–7 PM).

name: The Rising Sun

Reservations are available for lunch or dinner, and the site notes they do not accept reservations for drinks only.

name: The Three Hammers
description: The Three Hammers is a classic British pub in Hammers Lane, London, positioned as a great place to enjoy quality pub food with family and friends. name: The Clifton
description: The Clifton is a lovingly restored local British pub in London. It began life as a hunting lodge in 1846 before becoming a pub, and it has long been part of the local community, including hosting royalty—King Edward VII was said to use the rooms above the pub. In 2018, local brothers Ben and Ed, along with their childhood friend Adam, bought and restored it, creating a welcoming hub for families and visitors. The food focuses on fresh, local, seasonal ingredients with daily changing specials, and there’s also a curated selection of craft beers and spirits. The pub also runs a quiz night every Monday from 8pm.

name: The Duke Of York
description: The Duke of York is a traditional pub in the heart of St John’s Wood, London, minutes from Abbey Road Studios and right next to Lord’s Cricket Ground. It offers an inviting atmosphere for a meal and a pint, with classic pub dishes alongside some more modern options. The menu includes favourites such as hearty pie, classic fish and chips, a vegetarian option, and a Sunday roast. Alongside food, there’s a wide selection of beers, wines and cocktails. The pub also mentions private functions and is open from 11am Monday to Saturday and 12pm on Sundays.

name: Three Falcons Indian Gastropub
description: Three Falcons is a lively, friendly English pub in London, described as an “ultimate destination” for Indian food near Lord’s cricket stadium. It offers a fine dining Indian restaurant experience with a diverse menu of authentic flavours, alongside classic, quintessentially British food offerings with seasonal menus. The pub has a relaxed, welcoming neighbourhood atmosphere, with a wide range of local London craft ales, beers, select gins, classic Champagnes and curated wines. Upstairs are 23 recently re-furnished, fully en-suite bedrooms, with breakfast included. It’s also positioned as a venue for celebrations and business meetings.

name: Chandos Arms
description: The Chandos Arms is a friendly neighbourhood pub in Colindale. It’s known for big-screen sports, karaoke nights, DJs, bingo, and live music, creating a proper community atmosphere. The pub also serves fresh food daily, with a menu featuring burgers and pizzas made with fresh, high-quality ingredients. Kitchen opening times are listed for weekdays and weekends, and there are current opening times for the venue throughout the week.

name: The Beaufort

It offers parties and celebrations, with capacity for sit-down meals and drinks/canapés.

name: The Moon Under Water
description: The Moon Under Water in Colindale (10 Varley Parade) is open from early morning until late at night, with hours listed daily. name: Albert Arms

Food is served via resident Thai kitchen SAAWAROS, with a MAIN MENU in the first-floor restaurant and a BAR MENU in the ground-floor pub, plus famous Sunday roasts. Entertainment is mentioned as something they “often” put on, and bookings are recommended.

name: BrewDog
description: BrewDog Waterloo is a large, two-floor bar right by Waterloo Station, with nearly 1,800 capacity. It has 60 taps pouring fresh craft beer from an on-site microbrewery, plus a full restaurant menu (including burger, pizza, brunch and vegan options). Daytime offers coffee, brunch and co-working, along with interactive activities such as duckpin bowling, darts and ping pong. At night it becomes a late-night entertainment spot with live sport shown on Sky and across 11 projectors and 23 screens. There’s also a beer garden/outside tables, and the venue is dog friendly.

name: Bunch of Grapes
description: Bunch of Grapes is a traditional British pub in the heart of London Bridge, located near London Bridge station, Borough Market and the Shard. It serves British classics with seasonal ingredients, including a famous Sunday Roast, plus hearty pub food such as sausage and mash, fish and chips, bar snacks and burgers. The pub has a covered and heated sunny beer garden, and also features a “Cellar Tap” for vertical drinking with beers on tap and TV. It screens all World Cup 2026 games live and offers parties and events with delicious food and drink packages.

name: Camel & Artichoke

name: Coach House at the George

The venue is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it shows live football and rugby (including Six Nations) and other major events like the World Cup and F1. The pub is described as a “Hidden Gem of London” and features real ales, a beer garden, and live sports. It’s also listed as family friendly, with the option to book a table.

name: Dean Swift
description: Welcome to the Dean Swift Pub in Tower Bridge, just by historic Tower Bridge in Butler’s Wharf. The pub pours 20 craft beers, plus quality wines and spirits, and is known for hearty Sunday roasts, fish & chips and tapas. There’s an authentic tapas kitchen serving small plates alongside pub classics and sharing boards. The Sunday roast has been voted one of London’s Top 25 Sunday Roasts by the Evening Standard, with booking recommended. The upstairs party room is available for private hire. The venue also hosts a quiz night every Sunday at 6.30pm, and the page mentions an impressive array of beers and board games.

name: Doggett's Coat & Badge

The pub is described as a city-centre spot known for “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”, with British pub classic menus and options to book a table or order at table/for collection. It also highlights views across the river towards landmarks including St Paul’s and the Old Bailey. Opening hours run late most days, with weekend hours extending to midnight.

name: Flowers of the Forest

It has a good sized beer garden and offers a wide selection of worldwide lagers, beers and craft ales, plus wines, prosecco and champagne, and a range of spirits including many gins and vodkas. The venue also has a music setup with a jukebox, and it occasionally has live music. Guests can borrow a pool cue or set of darts to play, and the pub shows sports on Sky Sports, BT Sport, Racing UK and At the Races, following a range of football and other sports.

name: George Inn
