It offers food built around social sharing, including a seasonal menu with dishes such as fish and chips and pie and mash, plus Sunday roasts served from midday until they’re gone. The pub also has craft beers and cocktails, and it hosts events such as quiz night and themed food/drink nights. Sports fans can watch major football on big screens, including FIFA World Cup 2026 and the FA Cup Final. There are also comfortable ensuite hotel rooms and options for parties, weddings and private hire.

name: The Ashburnham Arms
description: The Ashburnham Arms is a traditional local pub in a quiet residential street in Greenwich, found in the Ashburnham triangle off Greenwich High Road. It has been serving the community since 1850, offering homely hospitality, hearty home-cooked food, wines, and award-winning real ales from Britain’s oldest brewery. The pub is described as a great spot for meals or drinks with friends, with a lovely patio to the front, a large garden to the back, and a charming conservatory area that brings light into the pub all year round. The venue also sits in an area linked to Edgar Wallace, the creator of King Kong.

name: The Coach and Horses
description: The Coach & Horses is a market pub in the centre of Greenwich’s famous market, near attractions like the Cutty Sark, National Maritime Museum and Royal Observatory. It’s described as steeped in royal history and popular with shoppers and tourists, with a welcoming atmosphere and “market garden” tables. The pub offers seasonal British menus, including Sunday roasts, vegan specials, and popular dishes like scotch eggs and bangers and mash. There’s also a covered terrace and a pub garden for drinks and catch-ups. The venue promotes watching major football events (FIFA World Cup 2026) with big screens and a proper pub atmosphere.

The pub also offers a range of drinks such as real ales, wines, and cocktails, and runs events like its Oyster Festival and parties in its private “Crows Nest” room. There’s a pub garden for spritz season, and the venue shows selected World Cup fixtures live, creating a shared-match atmosphere.

name: The Dial
description: The Dial is a modern, immersive pub with time-honoured beer and a lively atmosphere by London’s iconic peninsula. It offers food and drinks via its menus, plus opportunities to catch up with mates, watch sport, and enjoy live, local artists. The venue also promotes events such as game night and bottomless brunch, and it can be hired for private events like corporate parties and brand activations. There’s also emphasis on screens and a sports-bar feel for big games, alongside a micro-brewery offering beers made by Meantime.

name: The Gate Clock
description: The Gate Clock is a Wetherspoon pub in Cutty Sark for Maritime Greenwich, 210 Creek Road, Greenwich. It’s open daily from early morning until late (with Friday and Saturday closing at 1:00am). Facilities include Wi‑Fi, TV screens, a licensed outside deck/licensed outside area, baby changing, meeting facilities, and step-free access. The pub also highlights children’s meals priced at £4.99 and £5.75, served with a drink and fruit. The site’s history features a world-famous gate clock mounted by the double gates leading into the Royal Greenwich Observatory, installed in 1852 and described as the public face of Greenwich Mean Time.

name: The Gipsy Moth
description: The Gipsy Moth is a British pub with old-fashioned charm and a bohemian edge, offering a warm welcome in London. It’s described as being just a short stroll from the hustle and bustle of London, and it sits within view of the famous Cutty Sark. The pub is positioned as a laid-back yet memorable place for drinking and dining, with flavoursome food and an explorative drinks menu. Opening hours are listed for each day, and the page includes an online table booking link and contact details.

name: The Graduate
description: The Graduate is a sports pub in Greenwich, London, on the corner of Blackheath Road and Greenwich South Street (107–109 Blackheath Road, SE10 8PD). It has a fully stocked bar with two pool tables, a dart board and multiple large screen TVs showing Sky Sports, BT Sport and Amazon Prime Video. The pub hosts regular entertainment including drag cabaret on the 2nd Sunday of each month (with free entry) and Kaya’s Speedquizzing every Thursday. It also runs FIFA World Cup 2026 match showings as opening time allows, and has “Footie at The Graduate” match listings.

name: The Guildford Arms
description: The Guildford Arms, Greenwich is a neighbourhood pub known for great food, good company and warm hospitality. It’s a welcoming spot for drinks, Sunday lunch and relaxed meals, with “Perfect Sundays” featuring traditional, hearty Sunday roasts that can sell out (booking recommended). The pub also has a leafy beer garden tucked behind the building, described as a peaceful escape. Food highlights include a Robata Grill kitchen with grilled dishes, alongside classic pub favourites. The venue offers flexible spaces for parties and events, including private meals and wakes. Dogs are very welcome with water bowls and friendly attention.

description: The Observatory is a historic pub in North Greenwich, located at the heart of The O2. name: The Old Brewery
description: The Old Brewery is a unique, charming pub in the Old Royal Naval College, Greenwich, just a short walk from Cutty Sark. It’s described as a great place for celebrations, with a beautiful dining room featuring original brewing tanks for Meantime. The pub serves hearty British seasonal menus with brunch, lunch and dinner options, plus spirits, wines and locally brewed craft beers. There’s also an impressive garden/courtyard for laid-back drinks and catch-ups. The venue hosts events such as weddings and parties, and it shows selected World Cup fixtures live with a shared-match atmosphere.

name: The Pelton Arms
description: The Pelton is a friendly local pub serving real ales, Neapolitan style wood-fired pizza from Wandercrust, and Latin inspired street food from Afuego. It’s known for live bands and acts, with a busy programme of events including music nights and quizzes. The pub also offers guest rooms above the pub, and visitors can book a room via the site. Contact details and opening times are provided, along with directions to the venue.

name: The Pilot Inn
description: The Pilot blends contemporary comfort with rich history, offering a place to eat, drink and stay in Greenwich. It has a seasonal menu with refined pub classics made from fresh, seasonal ingredients, alongside a well-stocked bar featuring modern craft beers and cask classics. The venue also offers boutique accommodation near the O2 Arena, described as a base for exploring London. There are options for private events including business meetings, weddings and birthdays, plus features such as board games and big screen sports viewing. Accessibility and family-friendly facilities are listed, and assistance dogs are welcome.

name: The Plume of Feathers
description: The Plume of Feathers is the oldest pub in Greenwich, established in 1691. It overlooks Greenwich Park and is close to the Observatory and Maritime Museum. The pub is described as warm and friendly, with original claygate fireplace and features, maritime relics, and historical paintings, giving a country-pub feel in the city. Dining is available in a candlelit mirrored restaurant, serving freshly prepared meals, snacks and light bites, and a full fare menu, including traditional Sunday roasts with fresh seasonal produce. In summer there’s an award-winning garden for “al fresco” dining. The pub serves real ales, draught lagers, cider and bottled beers, and is listed in CAMRA’s Good Beer Guide.

name: The River Ale House
description: The River Ale House is Greenwich’s first micropub, created for lovers of beer and micropubs. It opened on 13th September 2017 and has won multiple “Pub of the Year” awards. The pub focuses on offering a range of beer styles at reasonable prices, with most beers sourced from local breweries around London & Kent, plus options from further afield. Alongside beer, it stocks ciders, gins, wines, and also whiskey and rum, each with tasting notes. There’s a regular Tuesday Folk Night from 8:30pm, and it’s a place to meet for Charlton home games before or after matches.

name: The Sail Loft
description: The Sail Loft is a Fuller's pub right on the river, offering fresh food and fabulous drinks with stunning views. You can drink or dine at the water’s edge on the outdoor terrace, or enjoy the panoramic cityscape from the first-floor dining area. The pub serves refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, and promotes a new Prix Fixe menu for 2026. It also caters for private events including business meetings, weddings, birthdays and corporate events. Facilities include accessibility lift and step-free access, plus board games and baby changing facilities.

name: The Spanish Galleon
description: The Spanish Galleon is a traditional English pub in the heart of Greenwich, just moments from the Cutty Sark. It offers a warm, inviting atmosphere with maritime memorabilia, plus a selection of terrific cask ales and a desirable wine list. The pub is family-friendly and explicitly dog-friendly, welcoming guests of all ages (and furry friends). It also has a function room called “The Crow’s Nest” on the first floor overlooking Cutty Sark, suitable for special occasions, work events, weddings and Christmas parties.

name: The Stargazer
description: The Stargazer is a Wetherspoon pub at The O2, Peninsula Square, Greenwich (SE10 0DX). It’s open daily from 10:00am until 12:15am, with a note that children under 18 can only be on the premises between 10:00am and 9:00pm. Facilities include Wi‑Fi, TV screens, a licensed outside deck, baby changing, and step-free access. The pub highlights its connection to astronomer Sir Edmund Halley, with local references to his star catalogue and the Edmund Halley Way near The O2. The menu is available via the Wetherspoon app, and there are children’s meals featured.

name: The Trafalgar Tavern
description: The Trafalgar Tavern is a quintessential British riverside pub in Greenwich, with picturesque views overlooking the Thames. Inside, it’s “adorned with artefacts and paintings” telling the story of Britain’s naval history, with rooms themed around iconic naval victories. Guests can enjoy a pub lunch, midday pint, or Sunday roast, with a seasonal menu including classics such as famous fish & chips. It also has an “iconic Nile Restaurant and Collingwood Bar”. Drinks include more than 20 beers on tap, a whiskey range with over 100 varieties, a gin collection, and signature cocktails. The page also highlights private events and gift vouchers.

name: The Yacht
description: The Yacht Greenwich is a picturesque, historic pub in London’s Greenwich, tucked down a quaint cobbled passage with nautical-themed interiors and views of the River Thames. It offers delicious pub food with seasonal specials, plus a wide drinks range and Greene King beers. The venue is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it shows live rugby (Six Nations) and live football, with big-screen match-day atmosphere. It’s also dog-friendly and family-friendly, with WiFi and takeaway available. The pub has function rooms for meetings and celebrations, and it’s described as a waterside pub with a welcoming local feel.

name: Ye Olde Rose and Crown
description: The Ye Olde Rose & Crown Greenwich is a traditional pub in Greenwich, first established during the reign of Queen Elizabeth I and rebuilt in 1888. It features cast iron fireplaces and a wood-panelled bar, with glimpses of its past throughout. The pub is dog-friendly and offers WiFi, coaches accepted and takeaway. Food is a key part of the experience, with a menu of small plates, pub classics and Sunday roasts, plus deals and dish highlights. There are also events to look out for, including a pub quiz, and it’s set up for big match occasions with big screens for the World Cup.

name: Duchy Arms
description: The Duchy Arms is a pub, restaurant and beer garden at 63 Sancroft Street, London. The site highlights a garden and roof terrace, plus an à la carte menu and Sunday roasts. It also offers bookings for parties and functions. The venue features a pool table, and it lists pub and kitchen opening hours, with the kitchen closed on Mondays. Contact is available by phone and email, and the pub provides directions and social links.

name: Old Red Lion
description: The Old Red Lion is a Grade 2 listed classic pub with wooden beams, low ceilings and a central island bar, with a pub on the site since 1750. It’s known for brilliantly kept ale and classic pub food, including a “best Sunday roast in Kennington” with meat, veggie wellington, roasties, seasonal vegetables and sides. The venue also has a large beer garden described as a hidden gem, plus a conservatory and cosy interior spaces for quiet dinners or special occasions. There’s a cracking quiz and a jolly landlord, and it’s promoted as the place to watch World Cup matches live with big screens and an electric atmosphere.

name: The Beehive
description: The Beehive is a privately owned local pub in Vauxhall, London, with a distinctive 16th-century Tudor-style exterior. It’s described as having an “explosive buzz” on cricket days and is just minutes from The Oval Cricket Ground and nearby Tube stations. The pub offers a craft beer selection, live sports on 7 high-definition screens, and a secluded beer garden. It also promotes “traditional pub grub” and cricket day BBQ’s, with a kitchen that “gears up to serve” classic comfort food. The venue is positioned as a welcoming community hub for drinks and meals before and after cricket.

name: The Black Dog
description: The Black Dog Freehouse is an award-winning pub on Spring Gardens, Vauxhall. It serves rotating Cask-Marque accredited real ales, craft lagers, and a thoughtful wine list. The pub also offers fantastic food made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, with a menu that changes daily to feature seasonal dishes.

name: The Dog House
description: The Dog House is a grand old Victorian corner pub on Kennington Cross in South London. It has a horse-shoe bar serving a cracking range of beers, liveners and pick-me-ups. The pub features local art and curiosities, with plenty of cosy or lively spots to enjoy a pint. It’s known for its terrace with sunny spots, a heated stretch canopy, live sport, and lots of seating for big groups. The venue is open really late, and it’s a short walk from the underground.

name: The Jolly Gardeners
description: The Jolly Gardeners in Vauxhall is a Victorian, high-ceiling pub renovated and revived by five childhood friends. Opened in 2021 as a community hub for locals, it combines a bright, natural-light space with outdoor and indoor seating, including a “secret garden” suntrap. The pub features a stunning original timber bar, marble Victorian fireplaces, and a piano in the dining room. Food is a standout with a seasonal changing menu, sharing plates, mains, and roasts (including family-style and plant-based options). Drinks include south London brewed beers on draught and a comprehensive wine list. DJs and late-night vibes are mentioned for outdoor seating.

name: The Pilgrim
description: The Pilgrim Pub is a lively London pub in Kennington with two inviting beer gardens and a vibrant atmosphere. It offers live music, daily happy hours, and hosts events such as birthdays, corporate drinks, sporting events and special occasions, with large indoor and outdoor space. The pub also has a kitchen serving food on multiple days, with kitchen hours listed Monday to Friday and at weekends. It’s a great local spot for catching the big game and celebrating with friends, with booking enquiries available for functions.

name: The Prince of Wales
description: The Prince of Wales is a traditional independent pub set on leafy Cleaver Square in Kennington, offering open space in the city. It has a beautiful, cosy interior with eclectic artwork, plus a small seating area outside at the front. Food is served Wednesday to Sunday, including a Sunday Roast, with an all-day menu and Sunday menu available. It’s also described as a great pre-match spot when cricket is being played at The Oval nearby, for chatting and mingling before heading to the ground. The pub is known for a warm welcome and friendly clientele.

name: The Tommyfield

It also offers Sunday roasts (free-range) plus vegan and vegetarian dishes. The pub has a private Master Room with its own bar for parties and events, and it hosts stand-up comedy club nights through Always Be Comedy, with gigs held multiple times a week. Upstairs there are six bedrooms, each with its own character and amenities such as Egyptian cotton linen, HD Freeview TV, free Wi‑Fi, and Nespresso.

name: The White Bear
description: The White Bear is a historic Kennington pub “since 1780”, serving great beer and ales alongside British seasonal pub classics. The menus highlight locally sourced ingredients and dishes such as Venison Wellington, Sunday roast dinners, and vegan specials, with options including Chalk stream trout, West country beef and Hertfordshire game. The venue has a traditional-meets-modern look with eclectic art and an original wooden bar, and it’s a short walk from Oval Cricket Ground and Kennington Station. There’s also a Garden Restaurant, a private dining room and snug spaces for parties. The pub shows selected World Cup fixtures live and has a pub garden for drinks.

name: The Crown
description: The Crown Lee Tavern is a community pub in Lee, South-East London, blending local heritage with modern pub culture. It serves craft beers, Young’s cask ales and an extensive wine selection, and is known for Sunday roasts. The pub has a fab beer garden and offers spritzes and cocktails. It’s also a sports-focused venue showing Premier League, FA Cup and FIFA World Cup 2026 action, including England matches, with an electric match-day atmosphere. There’s mention of a newly-refurbished Francis Baring room for private screenings, plus spaces for parties and events such as weddings and celebrations of life.

name: The Lord Northbrook
description: The Lord Northbrook is a stylish Victorian pub in the heart of leafy Lee, serving first-class beers and delicious food. It’s described as a long-established community favourite and was refurbished recently, with a “brand new Lord” and a new menu. The pub offers dining with refined pub classics made from fresh, seasonal ingredients, plus a well-stocked bar featuring modern craft beers and cask classics. There’s also support for private events and a “What’s On” section, including live sport where you can watch live games and book ahead. The venue lists accessibility features and family-friendly facilities.

name: The Summerfield
description: The Summerfield is a cosy, family-run pub with a welcoming atmosphere and friendly staff. It features open fires and offers fresh stonebaked pizzas (7 days a week, 12pm–9pm) available for delivery/collection via Deliveroo or by calling. The pub also runs live entertainment every weekend, with quiz nights, and shows Sky & BT Sports on 5 screens. There’s also a weekly Summerfield Thai Night every Thursday from 6pm, with dishes such as Pad Thai, Green Curry and Soft Shell Crab. The venue can be booked for private functions and hosts special events.

name: Station Hotel
description: The Station is a lovely local pub & rooms on the doorstep of Hither Green railway station. There are 16 (oh-co-cosy) bedrooms for London minibreaks, weekend getaways and business trips. The pub also promotes community events and shows live sport on its TVs, including Six Nations rugby, World Cup football and tennis. name: The Dacre Arms
description: The Dacre Arms is a traditional pub in a quiet residential area on the border of Lewisham, Lee and Blackheath. It dates back to 1864 and was remodelled in the 1970s, with an unspoiled interior featuring an old public bar and saloon bar, separated into sections with a central servery. Visitors highlight the well-kept ales, including cask ales, and a cosy, old-school atmosphere. There’s also a well-appointed beer garden at the back, with a covered smoking area and an outside bar. The pub is described as not serving food, but offering bar snacks.

name: The Fox & Firkin
description: The Fox & Firkin hosts a busy programme of music and events, with listings including dub/reggae and DJ nights, plus a “Firkin Good Beer Festival” and other block party-style gatherings. The venue also has distinctive hire spaces: a 1950s Kent and East Sussex first-class train carriage (“The Firkin Express”), an outdoor “Garden” described as an urban oasis, and “The Bar”, a historic South London spot where you can grab a beer from their own brewery. name: The Watch House

It also promotes live World Cup match viewing with big screens and an “electric atmosphere”.

name: Skehans
description: Skehans is an independent, family-run pub in South London with a friendly traditional front bar. It has a wood-burning stove kept burning in winter, plus pool and darts. The pub is known for live music six days a week and hosts regular events such as jam sessions, trad sessions, writers’ circles, quiz nights, karaoke/live rock’n’roll, and Sunday folk sessions. Food is available via chai’s garden Thai (served daily 5–9:30pm), Chico’s Sunday roast (Sundays 12–4pm), and a Staropramen burger night (Tuesdays 5–9pm). There’s also an outdoor smoking area and a hidden garden at the back.

name: The Little Crown
description: The Little Crown is a friendly local pub where you can sit and relax with friends for a drink. It offers a wide selection of drinks, including worldwide lagers, beers and craft ales, plus frequently changed seasonal specials. There’s also a range of wines, spirits and many gins and vodkas, with some spirits available to be doubled up. The pub regularly features live music, disco and entertainment, and you can also enjoy sports and a juke box. Sports are shown on Sky Sports, TNT Sports, Racing UK and At the Races, covering premiership and international football, GAA, rugby, cricket and golf. Located in Deptford on New Cross Road.

name: The Rose
description: The Rose in New Cross Gate is a family-friendly pub known for great drinks, delicious seasonal food and “absolutely the finest pizza in South East London”. It has an awesome beer garden described as a New Cross right of passage, plus a beautiful interior for meeting friends and family for drinks, a bite, or both. The venue also boasts two private hire rooms for parties. There’s a “secret cocktail bar” upstairs with velvet booths, curated playlists and craft bartenders, and the pub offers gastro pub classics, pizzas and hand-crafted cocktails. Dogs are welcomed (“we LOVE doggos”).

name: The Shirker's Rest
description: The Shirker’s Rest is an award-winning independent micropub in New Cross (SE14), recognised as the Lewisham area CAMRA Pub of the Year 2026. Established in 2022, it’s been included in CAMRA’s Good Beer Guide every year since opening. The pub focuses on a warm welcome and top-quality cask and keg beers from independent breweries, plus proper cider, wines, spirits and soft drinks. A “snack wall” is available with pint accompaniments, and you can order Yard Sale pizza for something more substantial. It’s dog friendly, has air conditioning, outside seating, and an upstairs function room for hire (no fee, no minimum spend or deposit).

The menu changes daily and caters for dietary requirements. The pub is family friendly and welcomes dogs, and it has a “secret garden” for outdoor space. Sports fans can watch Sky Sports and BT Sport, and there’s a Tuesday pub quiz at 7:30pm. Kitchen and bar hours are listed on the site.

name: Kanpai
description: Kanpai is described as the UK’s first sake brewery, crafting modern British sake using traditional Japanese techniques since 2016. The venue is a sake taproom and includes a sake bar & kitchen, plus a sake shop. It offers small-batch, high-quality, sulphite-free, gluten-free, preservative-free, vegan options. Visitors can book table reservations, join sake tastings (each Saturday) and hands-on experiences on select Fridays, and buy award-winning sake direct via an online shop. The taproom is at 48 Druid Street, London Bridge (SE1 2EZ), under 10 minutes’ walk from London Bridge Station, and the Peckham premises are permanently closed with a move to London Bridge.

name: The Angel Oak
description: The Angel Oak in Peckham (formerly known as The Rye pub) is a historic pub on the corner of Peckham Rye Park, combining “old and new” for an atmosphere throughout the week. It’s positioned as a food destination with seasonal specials, pub classics, Sunday roasts, and a new Prix Fixe menu (two courses £18, three courses £22, 12–8pm Monday–Thursday). There’s also a Beer Garden with heaters and covers in winter, plus an outdoor BBQ and bar in summer. The pub promotes World Cup live viewing with a buzzing atmosphere, and lists Sky Sports and TNT Sports.

name: The Beer Shop
description: The Beer Shop London is a small, friendly micropub serving a rotating range of beer from independent breweries, available to drink in or takeaway. It’s described as a place to meet, chat, relax and enjoy good beer. The page also notes it is dog friendly and mentions upcoming events via an events page. Opening hours are provided, and there’s a note that the garden closes at 10pm.

name: The Greyhound
description: The Greyhound is an inclusive, socially conscious pub with a kitchen and a versatile basement venue, run by the people from The Cause. Located at 109 Peckham high street (SE15 5SE), it hosts an active programme of events including a weekly pub quiz every Wednesday from 8pm, plus live music and club nights featuring DJs and artists. There’s also a thoughtfully chosen wine list and a range of spirits behind the bar, including whisky, gin, rum and vodka. The page also invites visitors to check “What’s On Tap.”

name: The Long Pond
description: The Long Pond in Eltham is described as “Eltham’s Smallest Pub”, with a focus on great local beer. It offers home delivery of its beers in 5 litre mini-casks to the SE9 area (and also to Eltham, New Eltham and Mottingham, plus some peripheral locations). The page highlights several featured beers, including Wantsum Black Pig Porter, 9th Life IPA and Tonbridge Pond Life, with details such as ABV and hop notes. Opening hours are listed for each day, and the pub provides an option to order online or text orders for a callback.

name: The Park Tavern
description: The Park Tavern is described as a “proper London pub” with a comfortable, relaxing, informal atmosphere. It’s decorated and furnished in a style suited to the age of the building and is run on an old-fashioned landlord/lady principle, with an emphasis on sociable behaviour. The pub highlights a calm setting with light classical music and jazz in the background, and specifically says it has no TVs, sport, or pool tables. There’s a well-established rear garden for al fresco drinking and dining, with cover and heating, plus a front terrace for evening sunshine in a smoke-free environment.

name: White Hart
description: White Hart Eltham is a friendly local pub in Eltham, London, offering a go-to spot for favourite drinks. The pub has HD screens showing Sky and BT Sports, and it promotes watching every match live, including World Cup coverage. It also highlights live entertainment and live music, plus a cocktail menu and real ale. Facilities mentioned include a dartboard, pool table, Wi‑Fi, and an outside area. The venue is described as dog friendly, and it has a late licence, wheelchair access, and children welcome.

name: Chelsea Ram
description: The Chelsea Ram is a cosy, characterful pub and gastropub on Burnaby Street in Chelsea, London, with a welcoming local feel and “traditional charm with a modern twist.” It’s been on Burnaby Street for over a hundred years and is known for delicious drinks and mouth-watering dishes, including Sunday roasts and seasonal pub menus. The pub also offers spritz options on its “Spritz Season” menu. There’s an Ashburnham private room for parties and events, with its own private bar and a wall-mounted flat-screen TV. The venue also promotes World Cup 2026 match-day viewing with small plates and booking spots early.

name: Hollywood Arms
description: The Hollywood Arms is a historic pub in the heart of Chelsea, just a short walk from the Kings Road and Stamford Bridge. It’s known for a lively atmosphere on Friday and Saturday nights, with hangover-banishing Bloody Marys and indulgent Sunday roasts. The Boulevard Bar offers a gin & cocktail lounge feel with vibrant decor and floor-to-ceiling windows. The pub also promotes big-screen match-day vibes for the World Cup and runs seasonal spritz and food menus. There’s a Boulevard Room suitable for events, including weddings, with private bar and catering options.

name: King's Arms
description: The King’s Arms is a traditional pub in Chelsea (Fulham Road) known for live sport and a relaxed, friendly atmosphere. It’s described as a great spot for pre- and post-match drinks near Stamford Bridge. The pub serves great British pub food from a fresh, seasonal menu, alongside local craft beers and seasonal cocktails such as spritzes. There are big screens for key matches, including coverage for the Premier League highlights and the FIFA World Cup, with an “action-packed” match-day atmosphere.

name: Lots Road
description: Lots Road is a lively Chelsea destination gastropub tucked between Stamford Bridge and Imperial Wharf station. It’s known for a warm, welcoming atmosphere, friendly team and top-tier service. The kitchen serves seasonal menus with modern British dishes, elevated pub classics, and “the best Sunday lunch,” including roasts. At the bar you’ll find a great selection of beers, including cask ale, plus an impressive wine list and standout cocktails. There’s also a private room available for hire for birthdays, work events and family gatherings, and it’s described as a calm midweek spot to work with a laptop and coffee (or pint).

name: The Fox and Pheasant
description: The Fox & Pheasant is described as “a little country pub” tucked away in a corner of Chelsea. The site highlights both food and drinks, with links to a food menu and wine & cocktails. There’s a conservatory restaurant under a glass roof for dining reservations, alongside a pub area for drinks and bar snacks. The pub also offers private dining and a private dining room/conservatory exclusive for events. Booking information includes sitting times for lunch and dinner, and notes that guests must order at least one main course per person for dining.

name: The Pembroke
description: The Pembroke is a historic pub and lounge in the centre of Earl’s Court on Old Brompton Road, minutes from Earls Court and West Brompton stations. It’s positioned as “the home of the action” with live World Cup moments, plus pub quizzes and live sport. The pub offers a Prix Fixe menu (two courses £18, three courses £22) served 12–8pm Monday–Thursday, and it also promotes craft beer. Facilities include Sky Sports and TNT Sports, WiFi, and it has a rooftop beer garden. There’s also a private function room for events.

name: The Sporting Pages
description: The Sporting Page is a Chelsea sports pub on the corner of Camera Place, described as a hidden gem for sports fans. It has plenty of screens showing live sport, including Sky Sports and TNT Sports, making it a place to watch the Premier League and football near Stamford Bridge. The pub also offers great beers on tap and an “outstanding kitchen residency” from Dulwich Pantry, positioned as ideal for drinks before and after Chelsea home games. The page also includes a “WATCH TogetheR” section and a reservation option.

name: Duke of Cambridge
description: The Duke of Cambridge in Battersea is a local pub “home from home” with roots going back to 1890. It’s moments from Battersea Park and the Power Station, serving a seasonal British menu, a well-kept pint, and chilled drinks behind the bar. The pub is known for Sunday roasts with family-style roasting, and it also offers a private dining room for dinner parties and events. There’s a Wednesday pub quiz, and the venue shows the FIFA World Cup on big screens, plus TNT sports with big screens and a big atmosphere. Dogs are welcome, and you can book spots for matches and roasts.

name: Fox and Hounds
description: The Fox & Hounds is an atmospheric Victorian corner pub in Battersea, described as buzzy, friendly and traditional. It offers a Mediterranean-inspired seasonal menu alongside a quick pint option. The pub is noted as cosy and warm in winter, and it has a rose-clad garden in summer. The venue is also described as having an open kitchen for its food, and it hosts beer festivals and brewery-led events, plus good wines. There’s a “What’s on” section for this month’s events, and a gallery to discover more about the pub.

name: Hawkins Forge
description: Hawkins Forge is a quirky, multi-level British pub in London, described as a one-of-a-kind spot in Battersea near Clapham Junction and the River Thames. The venue features stylish ’70s-inspired seating, exposed brickwork and wall art nodding to its blacksmithing past. The pub offers mouthwatering food, a rotating selection of craft beers, and an adventurous cocktail menu. It’s also home to London’s first Arrowsmiths interactive darts experience, with darts and pub quizzes mentioned, plus live music as part of the entertainment. Opening hours are listed across the week, and it has an online table booking option.

name: St John's Tavern
description: St John’s Tavern is a modern craft beer pub in Clapham Junction, described as a friendly local with a welcoming atmosphere. It features an impressive selection of twenty taps, including local microbrews, innovative collaborations and classic ales, plus a drinks menu covering wines, spirits and cocktails. Food is a key part of the offer, with a diverse pub menu including fish and chips, bangers and mash, gourmet burgers and freshly made pies, as well as a pizza kitchen serving 20-inch 48-hour proved sourdough pizzas (including a vegan 14-inch option). The venue also has multiple large-screen TVs for watching live sports, and hosts weekly event nights such as pub quizzes and live music.

name: The Beehive
description: The Beehive is a friendly local pub in 197 St John’s Hill, London, aiming to be more than “just a pub” by making you feel at home. It supports the community, including local sports teams and art, and runs charity efforts such as 10p from items on its doggie menu going to HART Dog Rescue. The venue also welcomes waste oil recycling. There’s a sports focus with Sky Sports showing major sporting events, plus grassroots support. The pub offers booking for sporting events, quiz nights, wine clubs, and private hire, including parts of the garden and pub.

name: The Candlemaker
description: The Candlemaker is a community pub on Battersea High Street, known for great value and being a go-to spot for sport and big weekend entertainment. The venue has pool tables, dart boards, and a gaming machine, plus a lounge area with quality selected tunes. It hosts regular events including Live Sports on screens, open mic evenings, Reggae Thursdays, karaoke nights, DJs, and comedy nights. There are also themed nights such as a 90s party and a sea-shanty singing gathering for men aged 50+. The pub address shown is 136 Battersea High Street, SW11 3JR.

name: The Falcon
description: The Falcon is a historic pub in Clapham Junction (St. Johns Hill), described as a place for “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”. It offers British pub classic menus, with options to book a table or order at the table, for collection, and at home. The page also highlights loyalty and ale & gin trails, and notes the pub’s convenient location near Clapham Junction station and popular nearby attractions and landmarks around central London.

name: The Falconbrook
description: The Falconbrook is a cosy Battersea pub on the corner of Falcon Road, named after the river that once ran through Battersea. Formerly known as The Asparagus, it serves cracking pints and comforting classic dishes, with a menu of familiar favourites for brunch, lunch or dinner. The pub also offers a curated wine list and a friendly local atmosphere, just minutes from Clapham Junction. It promotes World Cup match viewing with big screens and an electric atmosphere, and runs Portobello Perks with discounted drinks from 4pm–7pm Monday to Friday.

name: The Junction
description: The Junction Clapham Junction is a traditional pub in the heart of Clapham Junction, formerly named the Windsor Castle. It’s known for its spacious beer garden and a family-friendly atmosphere, with bar games available. The pub offers a menu worth discovering, including pub classics and a hearty Sunday roast with all the classic trimmings. It’s also a sports-focused venue, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it shows live rugby and football, including Six Nations and live football across multiple leagues. Facilities include WiFi and takeaway.

name: The Latchmere
description: The Latchmere is a landmark Battersea pub known for well-kept ales, hand-crafted spirits, elegant cocktails, award-winning ales and fine wines. The menu is described as ambitious, featuring dishes such as a Scotch egg in black pudding, scallops with pancetta and horseradish gazpacho, plus Sunday free-range roasts and responsibly sourced fish. Vegan and vegetarian options are highlighted. The pub has garden spaces including a heated courtyard (covered in winter), an al fresco snug and a sun terrace. The first floor is home to Theatre503, an Olivier award-winning theatre for over 30 years.

name: The Lighthouse
description: The Lighthouse is a Battersea pub known for “top-notch pub grub”, seasonal dishes, quality wines, and locally brewed beers. It has a south-facing walled garden described as a sunny, secluded year-round hideaway, with a retractable roof plus blankets and heaters for bad weather. The venue is also party-ready, with bookable spaces including the garden and a Fireside room. Sports fans can watch major events on big screens, including the Six Nations, Premier League, Champions League, TNT Sports, and England matches during the 2026 FIFA World Cup. There’s also a board games area with games like chess, Scrabble, and Connect Four.

name: The London and South Western
description: The London and South Western is a Wetherspoon pub on Lavender Hill in Clapham Junction, Battersea (SW11 1LJ). It’s open late, with opening times listed daily and a note that children under 18 can only be on the premises between 8:00am and 9:00pm. Facilities include Wi‑Fi, TV screens, step-free access and a licensed outside area (deck). The page also includes a “Pub history” section, saying it opened c1935 as Hastings Ltd’s flagship furniture store, before becoming a pub. There’s a children’s menu (£4.99 children’s meals) and information about Wetherspoon app ordering.

name: The Lost Society
description: Lost Society is an art deco-inspired venue offering “Eat, Drink & Dance With Us”, with new food and cocktail menus and a redesigned interior. The site highlights a la carte dining, Saturday brunch, and Sunday roast, alongside drinks. It also promotes a lively atmosphere with “good vibes” and private hire availability on Monday–Wednesday. Opening hours vary by day, with later closing times on weekends. The venue is located at 339 Battersea Park Road, Battersea, London (SW11 4LS), with nearby stations including Battersea Power station and Battersea Park/Queenstown Road rail.

name: The Magic Garden
description: The Magic Garden in Battersea Park Road, London (SW11 4LG) is a venue with late opening hours and a busy events calendar. It hosts featured and upcoming free-entry shows such as World Music Method Presents Sergio Marciano’s Latin Bridge (Cuba), a Pub Quiz, and an Open Jam Night (Mood Jam). The pub also lists a disco event with tickets. The page includes a “Food” section link, and offers reservations via an online booking link. Overall, it’s presented as a music-and-events-focused pub with long evening trading.

name: The Merchant of Battersea
description: The Merchant of Battersea is a lively neighbourhood pub in Battersea/near Clapham Junction, described as “the home of the action.” It’s positioned as a go-to spot for sport and live music, with events every night and a warm, welcoming vibe. The page highlights an “incredible atmosphere for live sport” and links to fixtures and what’s on. Facilities listed include Sky Sports/TV and TNT Sports, plus WiFi. It also mentions being dog friendly and family friendly, and offers table booking. Serving hours are shown daily, with later opening on weekends.

name: The Northcote Saviour
description: The Northcote Saviour on Northcote Road in Battersea is a bar and all-day dining spot serving fresh bites and beers. The menu includes classics with creative twists, with options such as double cheeseburger, BBQ and small sharing plates, slow-cooked lamb shoulder, calamari fritti, Tuscan meatballs, and lunchtime flatbreads. A standout feature is churros (“Porras”) in an Andalusian style, served with Spanish hot chocolate dip. The bar also offers craft beer, wines, cocktails, and barista coffee, plus alcohol-free beers and cocktails. There’s no outdoor table reservations, and seating outside is limited after 10:30pm.

name: The Plough
description: The Plough is a craft house and kitchen with an American twist, offering a long list of craft & bottled craft beers plus spirits, cocktails and wines. It’s open daily from brunch till late, serving burgers, saucy wings and fresh veggie options. The pub is positioned as Clapham Junction’s go-to for long lunches, after-work pints and sunny evenings, with a buzzy atmosphere. It also promotes live sport with screens for major sporting moments, and it shows FIFA World Cup 2026 games. There are spaces for events and meetings, plus fast WiFi for remote working.

name: The Prince Albert
description: The Prince Albert is a traditional pub with a grand corner position, charming locals since 1866. It sits opposite the entrance to Battersea Park, near Albert Bridge, offering a sanctuary from the bustle for drinks and seasonal British food. The well-stocked bar includes a great selection of beers and an eclectic wine list, with menus featuring items like homemade pies and a famous Sunday roast. The pub also has party spaces including the Bridge Room and a heated, covered Royal Garden. It hosts World Cup screenings both inside and out, with drinks packages and food.

name: The Rose Battersea
description: The Rose Battersea is a stylish modern gastropub and a local favourite, known for mouthwatering dishes and an impressive drinks selection. It’s presented as a welcoming place to unwind after work or catch up with friends. The page highlights offers including Happy Hour (2-for-1 drinks on specific days and times) and an all-day Sunday Roast with meats, crispy potatoes, seasonal vegetables and rich gravy. For weekend entertainment, it also advertises Late Nights with live DJs every Friday and Saturday from 8pm until late. The page includes imagery suggesting a beergarden and sports-themed visuals.

name: The Woodman
description: The Woodman in Battersea is described as a traditional English country pub tucked among Battersea’s backstreets. It’s known for a cosy, intimate atmosphere with oak barrel tables, stock-piled logs, candlelit corners and a classic centre-piece bar. The pub also has a quirky courtyard garden described as a peaceful outdoor haven. The venue offers real ales and fine wines, along with friendly hospitality. The page encourages guests to “Eat with us” by calling to book a table, and it also invites enquiries for functions and events.

name: Balham Bowls Club

name: Hagen & Hyde
description: Hagen & Hyde is a pub on Balham High Street in South London, known for a great atmosphere and lots of live music. It has a towering bar serving everything from standard after-work pints to late-night drinks. The pub also hosts a pub quiz every Monday. For food, it recommends its “big sisters” menu at Balham Bowls Club and has teamed up with Yard Sale Pizza to deliver pizza straight to your table (with a menu link provided).

name: Regent
description: The Regent is a fun-loving neighbourhood pub in the heart of Balham. It offers pints, cocktails and sharing plates, with a relaxed front room for dining and drinks and a back room that buzzes with live sport, music and quizzes. Out back, there’s a “secret garden” that works as a cosy winter escape and a sun-soaked summer hangout. Sundays feature epic roasts and quiz buzz, while the rest of the week is for easy catch-ups, great food and lively nights. The page also mentions a cocktail club deal and links to a “What’s On” page.

name: The Bedford
description: The Bedford is a pub, club, restaurant, live music and entertainment venue in Balham. First built in 1931, it underwent a multi-million pound refurbishment. The venue has five bars serving artisan spirits, craft beers, cocktails, wine and Champagne. Its restaurant focuses on British Isles ingredients, with responsibly sourced fish and vegan/vegetarian dishes. There are spaces to party including a Ballroom and Cocktail Bar, plus an iconic stage in the Club Room that has hosted artists such as Ed Sheeran and Sam Smith. The Bedford also offers 15 boutique bedrooms with luxury features like Hypnos beds, Egyptian cotton linen, roll top baths and rain showers.

name: The Cyclist
description: The Cyclist is a modern British pub in Balham, just across the road from Balham Station. It offers an all-day food offering during the week, plus Saturday brunch and Sunday lunch at weekends. The food approach focuses on seasonality, with small plates, seasonal specials and hearty gastropub classics, and menus are available to explore. The venue also has a hidden upstairs secret cocktail bar with velvet booths, curated playlists and a cocktail menu featuring drinks like the French Martini and Smoked Old Fashioned. There’s also a games section and features such as a terrace, Sunday roast and a pub quiz.

name: The Devonshire
description: The Devonshire in Balham is a lively, week-long hotspot with a focus on food, drinks and events. The pub promotes “The Balhamas” vibe, including brunches, cocktails and DJs, plus live music. It has a standout pub garden with an outdoor bar serving spritzes, daiquiris and pints. Food includes a Burger Shack, pub classics and seasonal menus, with Sunday roast dinners served by Head Chef Raff. The venue is also described as a rugby HQ and sports spot for major tournaments, with big screens and match-day atmosphere. Events listed include weekly quiz nights and Women’s Six Nations fixtures.

name: The Grove
description: The Grove is a pub in Balham, tucked just off Balham High Street, established in 1870. It offers “Food & Drink” with classic British pub menus that change with the seasons, including vegan and allergen-friendly options, plus lighter bites, coffee and pastries. The pub is open daily (Sunday 11am–11pm) with food served 12pm–9pm. It’s a popular spot for big-match rugby screenings and Sunday roasts, and there’s a sun-soaked beer garden and light, airy indoor spaces. The venue also hosts parties and events, with flexible indoor spaces and seasonal sharing boards and summer plates.

name: The Nightingale
description: We’re a proper community pub, proudly serving Balham locals and anyone who fancies a great pint just a short stroll from Clapham South and Wandsworth Common. Built on the Old Park Estate back in 1853, The ‘Gale is a mid-Victorian, cottage-style pub and a Grade II listed building, packed with character and a few stories of its own.

name: Coach and Horses
description: The Coach & Horses is a cosy, “wonky” proper pub in the heart of Barnes High Street, moments from Barnes Green and a short stroll from the river. It’s known for hearty, properly British pub grub with fresh, seasonal classics such as pies and roasts, plus a Burger Shack serving burgers straight from the garden. A major highlight is its huge beer garden with plenty of seating, cosy hut areas, and TVs for live sport. The pub also hosts lively garden parties and community events, and it’s dog friendly with water bowls and treats. There’s also mention of staying nearby in a Young’s room.

name: Red Lion
description: Set on the village crossroads, The Red Lion serves honest food and beautifully kept beer in a setting shaped by centuries of local life. Guests can take a seat by the fire or head out to the leafy garden, with lights, trees and a relaxed atmosphere in Barnes. The pub offers a dining menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, with children’s menu available until 6pm. There’s also a new prix fixe menu for 2026 and options for private events, including garden bookings and a large dining space. The venue is family-friendly, has a real fire, and offers accessibility features and free WiFi.

name: The Bridge
description: The Bridge in Barnes is a foodie pub, restaurant, walled garden and hotel in leafy Barnes. It’s described as a friendly local spot for weekday lunch or a cosy dinner in front of the open fire in the historic Boathouse Dining Room. The pub is renowned for hearty Sunday roasts, with menus featuring fresh ingredients and home-cooked treats. Guests can enjoy good quality local ales, craft beer and a Spritz menu. There’s a walled beer garden, and the venue offers restaurant and garden hire for weddings and events, plus eight boutique hotel bedrooms.

name: The Brown Dog
description: The Brown Dog is an independent, locally owned pub and dining room tucked away in the back streets of Barnes (“Little Chelsea”, South West London). It focuses on high-quality food in the comforting surroundings of a pub, with a frequently changing seasonal menu served in-house. The venue also promotes pizza nights, stating it is open for pizzas every Tuesday, and shares new opening hours running from Wednesday through to Sunday. Booking is advised, with some tables kept for walk-ins. The site also highlights the pub’s community-focused approach and provides links to “eat & drink” and events.

name: The Bull's Head
description: The Bull’s Head is a South West London pub ideally located along the riverside, just a short walk from Barnes Bridge station, perched along the Thames. It serves seasonal British food from lunch through to supper, alongside a wide selection of wines, ales, craft beers and spritz. The pub is described as a historic London jazz venue, with weekly live jazz in an acoustically perfect Jazz Room. Inside, there are picture-perfect spaces including the Melrose Room with sweeping river views, plus cosy rooms for celebrations and private events. The pub also states it is dog friendly.

name: The Crossing
description: The Crossing is an independent pub in Barnes, established in 2021 and founded by Christian Arden. It has been completely refurbished with a light, cosy interior. The pub serves seasonal food alongside drinks, with a main menu and a Sunday roast/sunday menu. There are also sections for a drinks menu and events/functions, and it offers a “Friends of The Crossing” deal of 15% off your food bill Monday to Thursday. The venue is located at 73 White Hart Lane, Barnes, SW13 0PZ.

name: The Sun Inn
description: The Sun Inn is described as a historic, iconic London pub with a village atmosphere in Barnes, set by the riverside on the banks of the Thames. The page highlights “home-grown hospitality” and a warm welcome, positioning the pub as a place for a memorable drinking and dining experience. A “View Menus” link is provided, suggesting food is available, alongside the pub’s focus on drinks and dining.

name: Ye White Hart
description: The White Hart is an iconic riverside pub in Barnes, London, with views over the Thames. It’s a popular spot for pints in the sunshine, celebrations and family visits, with seating options including benches along the river and tables on the terrace. The pub serves fresh, seasonal British dishes with regularly changing specials, including generous Sunday roasts. There’s also a first-floor private space for group dining and celebrations (30–70 guests). Dogs are welcome, and the venue hosts events such as watching the Football World Cup, with dinner and drinks available before fixtures.

name: Jolly Gardeners
description: Jolly Gardeners, Mortlake is a traditional pub with a good-sized beer garden. The building was rebuilt in 1922, replacing an earlier pub dating back to 1794, and it has historical links to the Three Tuns name (1720) and the current name appearing in 1796. It was originally a two-bar pub, with the separating screen removed in 1987. Inside, it has a pool table in the back room, two dartboards, plus a jukebox and fruit machines. The page also notes it is an ex Young’s house and is owned by Punch Pubs & Co. Opening hours run from noon to late each day.

name: Pig & Whistle
description: The Pig & Whistle is a well-known East Sheen pub with rooms on Sheen Lane. It combines a lively local bar with food service and practical accommodation in one convenient spot. The venue offers a sociable atmosphere, outdoor space, and a handy location for Richmond, Kew and surrounding parts of south west London. Amenities listed include family-friendly facilities, food served, pet friendly, a beer garden, cocktails, real ales, parking, live sports, and accommodation.

name: The Hare and Hounds
description: The Hare & Hounds is a proper community pub in East Sheen, serving seasonal, British pub food and a range of great drinks. It’s known for its “glorious” garden and beer garden atmosphere, with an outdoor bar and garden kitchen, plus cosy garden huts for private gatherings. The pub welcomes locals, families and “four-legged friends”, with dogs explicitly welcome. Food is served daily (12pm–9pm) and the kitchen supports relaxed lunches, Sunday roasts and summer dining. The venue also promotes community events and shows live football matches, including World Cup fixtures. There’s also accommodation via nearby Young’s rooms.

name: The Plough
description: The Plough is a traditional 18th century pub on the edge of the Royal Richmond Park in East Sheen. It’s a relaxed place to enjoy a perfectly poured pint of London Pride or a glass of wine, with options to join the bar or unwind in the lovely garden. The pub offers dining with a menu of refined pub classics made from fresh, seasonal ingredients, and it also hosts events. Features include a real fire, free WiFi, baby changing facilities, families welcome, historic pub character, and outside seating. Dogs are welcomed, and there is outside seating and a garden for a more relaxed visit.

name: The Ship
description: The Ship is a historic pub in Mortlake, opened in 1525 and famed for being on the finishing line of the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race since 1845. It’s described as a picturesque riverside pub with nautical ties, including a white and navy blue exterior, an open fire and timber floor. The pub offers a “delicious menu” with classics and seasonal specials, including British comfort food such as pies, Sunday roasts, sharing platters, and options including vegan, vegetarian and non-gluten dishes. It also has a beer garden (weather permitting) and is dog- and family-friendly. Sports fans can watch live Sky and TNT Sports, with big-screen match viewing and fixtures listed.

name: The Tapestry
description: The Tapestry Tapas Bar in Mortlake offers Spanish-inspired tapas, paella, and a drinks list, with a focus on food and atmosphere. The site notes the venue is refurbishing/temporarily closed, but celebrations and special moments continue, including bookings for private functions such as wakes and weddings (30+ guests). There’s an outdoor beer garden described as a relaxed spot with sangria, cold beer and tapas. Themed Brazilian evenings are advertised with lively music and dance performances. The venue also mentions a 75" TV screen for parties and presentations, and highlights popular dishes like chorizo with new potatoes, burgers, and picanha.

name: The Victoria
description: The Victoria is an award-winning independent gastropub in the heart of East Sheen, moments from Richmond Park. It blends the comfort of a traditional pub with the flair of a modern restaurant, offering inventive seasonal dishes alongside much-loved classics in relaxed, stylish surroundings. Guests can unwind by the fire in winter or in the leafy walled garden in warmer months, with a well-stocked bar serving craft beers, cocktails and carefully chosen wines. The pub also has six boutique rooms upstairs, making it a great place to stay as well as dine. Seasonal menus are freshly prepared on-site using fresh, ethically sourced British ingredients.

name: Bricklayer's Arms
description: Originally founded as The Waterman's Arms in 1826 to serve the local ship builders of Putney, our traditional London local has been serving the residents of Putney for almost 200 years.

name: Duke's Head
description: The Duke’s Head in Putney is a Victorian Grade II listed riverside pub known for celebrations and a lively atmosphere. It offers seasonal British pub food, including Sunday roasts and bar snacks, with food served from 12pm–9pm. The pub also runs a Summer Spritz menu and hosts events such as weddings (with spaces including the Wolsey Room and Rowing Club) and parties. Sports fans can watch the FIFA World Cup 2026 with key matches screened, and there’s an events calendar for additional supper clubs and activities. The venue is located at 8 Lower Richmond Road, Putney, London SW15 1JN.

name: Green Man
description: The Green Man is Putney Heath’s go-to pub, proud to champion local producers and farmers. It serves seasonal British food all day, including pub classics, contemporary dishes, small plates/light bites, and legendary Sunday roasts. The bar offers real ales, wines, spirits and cocktails. A key feature is its sun-dappled beer garden by Putney Heath, described as Putney’s biggest beer garden and a great spot to watch the World Cup, with matches shown inside and out on multiple screens. The pub is also described as dog-friendly, with complimentary treats and even canine IPA (water).

name: Jolly Gardeners
description: The Jolly Gardeners in London is described as a laid-back, homely place for drinking and dining. It offers flavoursome food and an explorative drinks menu, suitable for everything from a lazy lunch to a family dinner. The page also promotes booking a table online and mentions events such as World Cup and bank holidays via the “What’s On” section. The venue is located at 61–63 Lacy Road, Putney (SW15 1NT), with opening hours listed daily.

name: King's Head

name: Queen Adelaide

name: The Arab Boy

name: The Spotted Horse

name: The Telegraph

name: The Holland Tringham

name: The Pied Bull

name: The Shakespeare
description: The Shakespeare Victoria is a traditional British pub in Victoria, offering pub food and drinks in a warm, welcoming atmosphere. The venue is known for cask ales, craft beers and a selection of wines, with live performances and quiz nights. Food highlights include small plates, pub classics and a Sunday roast with classic trimmings. There are also facilities such as WiFi, disabled facilities, takeaway and functions, plus it’s described as a historic pub. The page also mentions dog-friendly and family-friendly. Opening and serving hours are listed, and there’s a “World Cup bookings” promotion with big screens.

name: The Thomas Cubitt
description: The Thomas Cubitt is a unique Georgian pub in the heart of Belgravia, a short walk from Victoria Station. Named after Thomas Cubitt, a master builder instrumental in developing Belgravia’s streets and squares, it’s described as a historic and handsome building on Elizabeth Street. The pub has a handsome bar at its heart, serving a carefully crafted drinks list for pints, cocktails and more. Upstairs, there’s a light-filled 1st floor restaurant with a seasonal menu of British classics, including grilled steaks, fish and chips, and a special Sunday lunch.

name: The Victoria
description: The Victoria is a 19th-century traditional pub in Victoria, offering real ales and classic British pub food in a family-friendly setting. It has a beer garden (weather permitting) and WiFi, and welcomes dogs. Sports fans can watch live action with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with fixtures and big rugby events like the Six Nations (including women’s) and other major tournaments. The pub also runs regular community-style events such as a pub quiz every Monday. With breakfast, Sunday roasts, and a menu worth discovering, it’s positioned as a comfortable “second home” for get-togethers and match days.

name: Travellers Tavern
description: The Travellers Tavern Belgravia is a family-friendly pub in Belgravia, ideal for a rest stop after a long day. It serves cask ales and traditional pub food, with a menu that includes pub classics, small plates, breakfast, and a Sunday roast. The pub also has a beer garden (weather permitting) and offers WiFi and disabled facilities. Sports fans can watch live rugby and football, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports available, plus big-screen match-day atmosphere. There’s also a “Spin to Win” promotion via the Greene King app and regular “What’s On” events.

name: Paxton’s Head
description: The Paxtons Head in Belgravia is a grade II listed Victorian pub, originally built in 1900 as a gin palace. It features a striking red brick interior with etched mirrors and original details, and is positioned right next to Knightsbridge station. The pub offers an “excellent range” of cask ale and classic British dishes, including seasonal specials and a Sunday roast. Facilities include Sky Sports and TNT Sports, WiFi, a dartboard, disabled facilities, and it’s both family and dog-friendly. There are also function rooms available for meetings and events, plus sports viewing and live match screenings for major competitions like the Six Nations and live football.

name: Tattersalls Tavern
description: The Tattersalls Tavern Knightsbridge is a traditional British pub tucked away in Knightsbridge, just three minutes from Knightsbridge underground station. It offers a menu worth discovering, with pub classics, small plates and a Sunday roast with classic trimmings. The venue is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it promotes watching live football and rugby (including Six Nations) plus big-screen match atmosphere. Facilities listed include WiFi, delivery, functions and TotSpot, and it’s described as dog friendly and family friendly. There are also booking options for tables, sports fixtures and functions.

name: The Alfred Tennyson
description: The Alfred Tennyson is a welcoming neighbourhood pub in Belgravia, named after Lord Tennyson and set on the cobbled streets of Motcomb Street. It offers an extensive drinks list, plus snacks, and in summer there’s a terrace for relaxing and watching the world go by. Upstairs, Alf’s is a refined restaurant serving British and French classics, with exceptional wines and martinis in an atmosphere designed for long lunches and celebratory dinners. The venue also supports private hire on both first and second floors, and hosts a full calendar of events across Cubitt House including live music, Burns Night and New Year’s Eve parties.

name: The Gloucester
description: The Gloucester in Knightsbridge is a historic pub licensed in 1835 and described as the only public haven left on the street. It commemorates the Gloucester Regiment and is just a short walk from Harrods and Harvey Nichols on Sloane Street. The pub offers a traditional English pub experience with a first-floor bar available for private hire, plus a dog-friendly, family-friendly welcome and free WiFi. Food is a key part of the offer, with a seasonal specials menu and Great British pub classics such as hand-battered fish and chips, pie and mash, and burgers, alongside vegan, vegetarian, non-gluten and kids choices. There are also function rooms for events.

name: The Grenadier
description: The Grenadier is a historic pub in Belgrave Square, described as a “landmark” and a hidden gem loved by locals and visitors. It offers a seasonal menu created in-house from scratch, with fresh seasonal dishes and pub classics, alongside a curated wine list. The pub also has a “stunning dining room” for bookings, suitable for receptions and banquets. Food hours are Mon–Sat 12:00–21:30 and Sun 12:00–21:00.

name: The Horse and Groom
description: The Horse & Groom is a cosy, traditional pub tucked away in a picturesque cobbled mews off Belgrave Square in Belgravia. It offers a warm welcome and an intimate atmosphere with traditional wood panelling and etched glass. The pub serves an extensive menu of wholesome “home cooked” food alongside hand-pumped ales, beers, spirits and wines. There’s an upstairs dining room that has hosted private parties, and an outside area in the mews for food and drink when the sun shines. The venue also has a long history (over 150 years) and is noted for appearances in films and TV, with famous neighbours and visitors mentioned.

name: The Star Tavern
description: The Star Tavern is a traditional London pub in Belgravia, recognised as one of the best pubs in the area. It’s award-winning and focuses on great service, good beers and home-cooked food. The pub offers a menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, and it also provides drinks with recognition in the Good Beer Guide across all 50 editions. There are facilities for private events, including business meetings, weddings and birthdays, and the venue features a historic setting with real fire, comfy sofas, free WiFi and board games. Assistance dogs are welcome and families are welcome.

name: Chequers Tavern
description: Chequers (The Chequers Tavern) tells a history story tracing its roots back to an alehouse called “The Mason Arms” near St James after the Great Fire of London in 1666. It describes Mason Yard, where stonemasons prepared stones for Westminster Palace, and how coachmen and grooms would wait and pass the time drinking ale and playing chequers—leading to the name “The Chequers Pub” and a sign depicting a chequers board. The page also links to other Shannon Pubs venues, including Ye Grapes in Mayfair and The Chequers Tavern in St. James’s.
