name: Davy's
description: Davy’s is a collection of wine bars across London, focused on great food, service and—above all—wine. The site says the business was founded in 1870 and remains a fully independent, family business. There are menus available and the venue hosts wine tastings and other events, including “live music” mentioned for upcoming events. A featured location is Vintners Lanes, described as a brand new, award-winning boutique 6-lane bowling alley in a historic setting, with a “mouthwatering menu” and drinks. The page also promotes private dining across London with many private dining rooms for exclusive hire.

name: The Golden Lion
description: The Golden Lion, St James’s is a historic pub originally built in 1762 and most recently rebuilt in 1900. It features stained glass windows and a dark wood interior, plus an upstairs “theatre bar” with memorabilia from the former St James’s Theatre nearby. The pub offers a seasonal specials menu and classic Great British pub food, including hand-battered cod and chips, sausages and mash, and pan-seared steaks, alongside an extensive drinks range. It’s family-friendly and dog-friendly, and there are function rooms available for meetings and parties. The venue also promotes big match viewing with big screens for events like the World Cup.

name: The Red Lion
description: The Red Lion in Mayfair is a historic pub serving the area for well over 200 years. It’s a great spot to relax after shopping along Regent Street, with street-side socialising outdoors. The pub offers dining with a menu of pies and toasties to go with your drink, and a well-stocked bar featuring modern craft beers and cask classics. Visitors can also explore the venue via the on-site gallery, and the pub welcomes families and assistance dogs. Opening times vary by day, and it’s located at 2 Duke of York Street, Mayfair, London.

name: Three Crowns
description: The Three Crowns Piccadilly is a welcoming Greene King pub in central Piccadilly, ideal for a bite to eat or a quick drink while exploring nearby Trafalgar Square and Whitehall. The venue has a comfortable interior with leather seats and a “Historic Pub” feel, plus Sky Sports and TNT Sports. Food is a key part of the offer, with a menu worth discovering, pub classics, small plates, and a Sunday roast. It’s also set up for sports fans, with live rugby (Six Nations) and live football shown on TV, and fixtures available for booking. Facilities include WiFi, disabled facilities, and it’s family friendly and dog friendly.

name: Tom Cribb
description: The Tom Cribb is a small, cosy, characterful pub in London’s West End, ideally placed opposite the Harold Pinter Theatre. It’s a popular pre- and post-theatre stop, as well as a convenient break for visitors to nearby attractions like the National Portrait Gallery and Piccadilly. Named after bare-knuckle boxing champion Tom Cribb (who fought between 1805 and 1811 and later became the publican here), the pub’s interior and an English Heritage plaque commemorate its boxing heritage. The pub also offers a tasty menu with pub dishes such as pies, burgers, fish & chips, and smaller plates like sausage rolls, Scotch egg, and hash brown potato puffs.

name: Crown and Sceptre
description: Crown & Sceptre is a traditional British pub on Streatham Hill in London, open every day. It offers a wide variety of beers and drinks, with specials and something happening regularly. The venue hosts weekly events including DJs and live bands, creating a lively musical atmosphere. A standout feature is its large beer garden, ideal for enjoying a pint in the sun. The pub also welcomes dogs. The site highlights its history, saying it was built in 1822 to celebrate King George IV’s reign, with stories from coaching days and other local curiosities.

name: Effra Social
description: Effra Social in Brixton is a lively pub with interactive darts, a karaoke room, and a jam-packed events schedule including comedy nights, pub quizzes, and themed nights. It offers menus with sharing platters, “picky bits” and pub classics, plus deals such as £4.95 pints (Mon–Fri until 7pm) and 2 for £15 cocktails. The venue has a huge covered outside terrace and a “pastel pergola” beer garden with heaters for colder months. The site also highlights Brixton’s music and culture, including David Bowie’s birthplace, and mentions private party bookings.

name: Hootananny Brixton
description: Hootananny Brixton is a legendary live music venue and club, established in September 2007. It hosts a wide range of music shows and club nights, with genres including Jungle, Disco, Post-Punk, Reggae, Highlife, House and Electronic. Set in a striking Victorian building, it’s known for its spacious beer garden, quirky interiors and welcoming atmosphere. Guests can relax in a second bar and there are two pool tables. The venue also offers delicious street food from its food stalls to complement the music.

name: Hope & Anchor
description: The Hope & Anchor is a lively pub between vibrant Brixton and trendy Clapham, known for London’s best pub garden out back. It offers drool-worthy pub grub including sharing plates and piled-high Sunday roasts, plus cracking cocktails, vibrant beers and more. The venue is set up for big match days and major tournaments like the Fifa World Cup 2026, with key fixtures shown live on big screens and a proper pub atmosphere. There are live DJs every Friday and Saturday night, and the garden includes options like a retractable roof seating area and private tiki huts to catch the game.

name: Prince of Wales
description: The Prince of Wales is a traditional-style pub with a warm, friendly atmosphere, serving quality drinks at affordable prices. It’s located in Brixton Hill, South London, in a residential neighbourhood just outside the main Brixton centre, giving it a more local, community feel rather than a busy high-street location. The pub is run by Paul and offers facilities including being dog friendly, having a garden/patio, and watching sports. It also supports holding a party.

name: The Hand in Hand
description: Hand In Hand Brixton is a traditional pub in London (61 New Park Road, Brixton) with a wide variety of drinks and “unbeatable” drink offers. It’s positioned as a great place to relax with a pint and has a lively atmosphere. The venue also promotes live match viewing, saying it will show every match live and highlighting World Cup 2026. Facilities mentioned include Wi‑Fi, HD screens, and sports coverage via TNT Sports and Sky Sports, plus “Live Entertainment”.

name: The Windmill
description: The Windmill hosts a busy programme of live music events, with gigs listed on multiple dates and evenings. Examples include Garagebashing Vol. 36, Hyperdense and Wish, Yessir, Speedial, The No Frills Folk Club, and other named bands and acts. Ticket prices are shown for several events, including some free entries (e.g., The No Frills Folk Club).

name: Tulse Hill Hotel
description: Tulse Hill Hotel is a boutique hotel and gastropub in Tulse Hill, minutes from Tulse Hill station. It offers nine en-suite boutique bedrooms, a cosy pub, and an on-site restaurant serving seasonal British food. The venue has a beer garden out the front and back, plus Sky Sports and TNT Sports. The page promotes a “World Cup” live sports atmosphere, a new Prix Fixe menu (12–8pm Monday–Thursday), and regular offers such as Wing Wednesday and Hello Friday Prosecco deals. It also lists upcoming events and provides facilities including a car park and WiFi.

name: White Horse
description: The White Horse is a popular boozer on Brixton Hill known for friendly service and a great atmosphere. DJs run from Friday to Sunday, with a 3am licence at the weekend. The pub serves delicious homemade food fresh seven days a week at sensible prices. There’s outdoor space with a courtyard out front and an additional “NEW ONE” out back, ideal for summer months. The site also highlights regular sports-style event viewing (e.g., 6 Nations and World Cup) and shows a variety of menus and cocktails.

name: Raynes Park Tavern
description: The Raynes Park Tavern is an effortlessly elegant, family-friendly pub built in 1904, perched directly opposite Raynes Park station in South West London. It’s dog-friendly and offers excellent transport links and local amenities. The pub has a beer garden (weather permitting) and features Greene King sport coverage with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, plus live match viewing such as Six Nations and live football. Facilities include WiFi, disabled facilities, and games such as shuffleboard and Bank Shot Shuffleboard. The venue also promotes pub food, with a menu worth discovering, deals, and highlights like Sunday roast. There’s a pub quiz every Wednesday.

name: Brompton Cross
description: The Brompton Cross is a beautifully refurbished local landmark in SW3, described as the “beating heart” of the Brompton Cross village and neighbourhood. It offers a Classic Pub experience with an extensive bar snack menu made with British produce, alongside a carefully selected range of craft beer, ale, wine, champagne and cocktails. There are live piano evenings every Thursday and Friday from 6pm. The pub also has private hire available and a cosy upstairs dining room open every day. Kitchen opening hours are listed across the week, supporting food service throughout the day and evenings.

name: Chelsea Potter
description: The Chelsea Potter is a traditional Great British pub in Chelsea, set on the famous Kings Road. The venue says its doors have been open since 1842. It offers pub food including pies, burgers, Sticky Toffee Pudding, and a Sunday roast with classic trimmings. There’s also a menu of small plates and pub classics, plus drinks worth toasting. The pub is family friendly and dog friendly, with facilities including Sky Sports and TNT Sports, WiFi, and delivery. It hosts sports viewing events such as Six Nations and live football, and promotes big-screen match-day atmosphere.

name: The Admiral Codrington
description: The Admiral Codrington is a Chelsea freehouse (EST.1830) that has reopened after an extensive restoration. The pub offers seasonal British food made with the finest local produce, with menus including an à la carte and a Sunday menu, and a kitchen serving food on multiple days. Guests can dine in the pub or in an al fresco dining room, and there’s also a covered outdoor seating area shown. The first-floor Navarino Room is available for private hire for events throughout the year, with capacity for seated and standing guests.

name: The Builder's Arms
description: The Builder's Arms is a much-loved pub tucked behind the hustle and bustle of the King’s Road. It’s said to have been built to house the builders of the nearby St. Luke Church, and today offers a welcoming bar area with a fireplace for cosy winter evenings. There’s also a comfortable restaurant and an outside terrace for sunnier days. The pub serves a blackboard menu of British classics throughout the day, with an à la carte menu available. The venue also runs events across Cubitt House, including live music on Wednesdays and Thursdays (listed for The Barley Mow).

name: The Bunch Of Grapes
description: The Bunch of Grapes, Knightsbridge is a historic pub built in 1644 on Brompton Road, set between Harrods and the Victoria & Albert Museum and near the Natural History and Science Museums. It’s described as a warm, wood-toned place with friendly bar staff and floor-to-ceiling windows for great light and people-watching. The pub highlights dining with “Delicious Pub Food”, including celebrated fish and chips and options for vegetarian, vegan and non-gluten meals. There are also function rooms available, plus free Wi‑Fi and a dog-friendly welcome. The page also mentions big match viewing with big screens for major events.

name: The Chalk Freehouse
description: The Chalk Freehouse is a refined British pub dining spot in the heart of Chelsea, just off the King’s Road. It’s a warm, welcoming venue with a relaxed, informal atmosphere across two floors, including an intimate open kitchen and a private dining room downstairs. The menus focus on seasonal British cuisine with reimagined pub classics, seasonal specials, and bold flavours, alongside a thoughtful selection of craft beers, fine wines, and standout cocktails. It’s described as a sister pub to The Hand & Flowers, built on proper food, warm hospitality, and great British cooking.

name: The Coopers Arms
description: The Cooper’s Arms is a newly refurbished Chelsea local just off King’s Road, offering “delicious drinks” and “fantastic food” with a classic pub vibe. The menu includes seasonal British pub classics such as fish and chips, burgers and a homemade pie, plus traditional Sunday roasts. There’s also a spritz menu for “Spritz Season” and match-day atmosphere for the FIFA World Cup 2026. The pub has multiple spaces for occasions, including the Albert Room for celebrations and private hire, a Snug, and Ruby’s Patch for group dinners. Outdoor garden seating is available for drinks and dining.

name: The Hunter's Moon
description: The Hunter’s Moon is a traditional countryside-style pub and dining room in South West London, offering a warm, welcoming atmosphere. It’s known for a modern take on classic countryside dining, with seasonal ingredients and classic British dishes. The well-stocked bar serves a fine selection of ales, wines and spirits, and there are bar snacks available all day. The venue has a restaurant and bar area with set lunch and dinner kitchen times, and it’s open daily with longer hours from Thursday to Saturday. The page also includes a sample menu and drinks menu, plus reservation booking.

name: The Phene
description: The Phene is an iconic Chelsea pub in a leafy enclave near the King’s Road, known for a cosy bar, beautiful private rooms and a gorgeous, heated and covered garden. With heritage stretching back to 1853, it offers quality food and drink in a relaxed, luxurious setting. The kitchen, led by Michelin-trained chef Sidy Kounta, serves classic British dishes using seasonal ingredients, with a reputation for phenomenal Sunday roasts and options including gluten-free, vegetarian and vegan offerings. There’s also a spritz menu, a curated wine list, and a football-free zone (no World Cup). The pub has meeting rooms and event spaces, including wedding celebrations with a full wedding licence.

name: The Phoenix
description: The Phoenix, Chelsea is a traditional pub in a relaxed corner of Smith Street, just south of King’s Road. It offers great British food, cask ales and seasonal cocktails, with modern and traditional options and regularly changing daily specials. Sunday roasts are a highlight, with roast meat, crispy roast potatoes and Yorkies. The pub also has a relaxing outdoor terrace and is described as Chelsea’s best community pub, near Sloane Square tube station, Chelsea Physic Garden and the National Army Museum. Sunday night includes a pub quiz with prizes, and guests can order food and drink to their table via the Young’s On Tap app.

name: The Pig's Ear
description: The Pig’s Ear is a countryside-style pub in Chelsea on Old Church Street, run by the Gladwin Brothers. It focuses on locally sourced produce with seasonal dishes, including generous roasts and options like pie and a pint by the fireplace, plus fresh seafood at an oyster station. The pub also has a strong drinks offering, with beers, cocktails and wines from the family vineyard in Nutbourne. It hosts community events such as the Flying Pigs Run Club and cocktail masterclasses, and it’s described as a place where locals gather and customers become friends.

name: The Surprise
description: The Surprise is a refreshingly independent, proudly local neighbourhood pub and local landmark since 1853 in Chelsea. It’s warmly welcoming and set just steps from world-class attractions and King’s Road. The pub offers an imaginative drinks menu and British-inspired cooking, with lunch and dinner served in both the restaurant and bar. There’s also a smart private dining space, The Hamilton Room, for get-togethers, celebrations and meetings, hosting up to 35 seated or 50 standing. The kitchen is described as serving simple dishes with locally sourced ingredients.

name: The Sydney Arms
description: The Sydney Arms is an independently owned Freehouse pub in the heart of Chelsea, offering a time-honoured welcome and a “pub at heart” atmosphere. It has deep roots in the horse racing community and is described as a premier destination for racing enthusiasts. The pub is set up for sports viewing with five high-definition screens showing major sporting events including rugby and football. Food & Drink includes a “Best of British” menu with dishes such as Steak Sandwich, Newmarket Musk’s Sausages, and Ale Battered Fish & Chips, plus a curated wine list, cask-approved draught beers and lagers, and fine spirits. A “Peter O’Sullevan Room” is mentioned for private bookings.

name: Belle Vue
description: The Belle Vue is a Clapham pub by Clapham Common tube, known for “good vibes” and “cold pints.” It’s a go-to spot for parties and events, with bookable spaces and options for arrival drinks. Sports fans can catch live action with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, including football, rugby, big fights, and major tournaments like the FIFA World Cup 2026, shown on big screens. The venue also has late-night energy with DJs and dance-floor vibes, plus a drinks focus including spritzes and cocktails. Walk-ins are welcome, and booking is available for the best seats.

name: Old Town Tavern
description: Old Town Tavern is a modern, neighbourhood-style pub with a great location and friendly staff. It offers a free-of-tie selection of 20 beers on tap, including local microbrews, innovative collaborations and classics, alongside quality wines, spirits and cocktails. The venue has a new basement games room and event space, with a pool table, smart darts, foosball and retro arcade machines. There are weekly event nights and specials, including Trivia Tuesdays and Thursday Tunes, which highlights great food, great beer and live music.

name: O’Neill’s
description: O’Neill’s is an “original Irish” pub brand offering a warm Irish welcome with “a pint of craic and a dash of charm.” The site describes a high street haven for a big night, a big match, or a big feast, with options for rounds, lunch, and breakfast. It also highlights “great food and live sport,” plus drinks offers, fantastic music, and live experiences across sport, music, and events. There are features like booking a table, ordering at table, and collection or delivery for food, and a “Find your nearest pub” section to locate local venues.

name: The Abbeville
description: The Abbeville is a rustic yet refined neighbourhood gastropub in Clapham, set at the heart of Abbeville Road. It’s known for British food made with quality ingredients from small producers, including free-range Sunday roasts, responsibly sourced fish, and vegan/vegetarian dishes. The pub has cosy snugs with an open fire in winter, and in summer the front doors open for al fresco drinking and dining. The drinks list includes local craft beers, artisan spirits, cocktails, and great wines. There are also themed offers such as Burger Monday, Steak & Wine Wednesday, and Pie & Pint Thursday.

name: The Alexandra
description: The Alexandra in Clapham is a lively pub known as “the home of the action”, with a buzzing World Cup atmosphere. It offers craft beers, signature craft cocktails and freshly baked stone-baked pizzas (eat in or takeaway). The venue has darts at its heart, including an interactive dart setup and a Darts Club bar, plus darts nights and darts-themed function room hire. Sports fans can enjoy Sky Sports and TNT Sports. It’s well placed near Clapham Common tube station and has WiFi. The facilities also highlight it as dog friendly.

name: The Bread and Roses
description: The Bread & Roses is a vibrant independent pub in the heart of Clapham, offering live music, theatre and comedy. It has a strong social-consciousness ethos and is an award-winning free house owned by The Battersea and Wandsworth Trade Union Council and run by the Workers Beer Company. The pub’s name references the 1912 “bread and roses” strike of women textile workers in Lawrence, Massachusetts. The page also highlights that it now has Sky & TNT for watching football, and it promotes its 2024 food and drink menus as being available online.

name: The King & Co.
description: The King & Co is described as a small but “perfectly formed” Clapham Common pub, tucked away from the main drag. It focuses on friendly, attentive service, an interesting and diverse drinks selection, and quality food. The pub runs £5 pints (Portobello Perks) Monday to Friday until 7pm. Food highlights include a rotating pop-up kitchen with street food, a Tagine and Grill special menu (Moroccan recipes), and Sunday roasts (beef, chicken, pork or veggie wellington). It also hosts regular acoustic nights and has big screens for World Cup live viewing, with a cosy, eclectic atmosphere and a front garden for summer drinks.

name: The Ox
description: The Ox is a gastro pub in the heart of Clapham, with a focus on provenance of produce. It offers seasonal British cuisine, along with a considered wine list and selected guest beers. The page also links to events such as Steak Night and Quiz Night, and includes directions to 50 Clapham High Street, SW4 7UL.

name: The Rose and Crown
description: The Rose & Crown is described as a “legendary pub” built for and around the local community, with an all-day dining and drinks menu. It offers a Public House & Dining Room and is open throughout the week, with kitchen hours running from midday through the evening (later on some days). The pub is located at 2 The Polygon, London SW4 0JG, and provides contact by email and phone.

name: The Stonhouse
description: The Stonhouse is a pub just off Clapham High Street, tucked away from the bustle. It has recently had a “magnificent makeover” and offers an elegant pub and garden setting. The venue is known for excellent cask-conditioned ales, a modern pub menu, a superb wine list and innovative cocktails. Food options include light bites, dishes to share, hearty mains and Sunday roasts. The pub says it works with small producers across the British Isles, with meat from high-quality suppliers, fish responsibly sourced, and vegan and vegetarian dishes.

name: The Tim Bobbin
description: The Tim Bobbin (also known as The Bobbin) is a neighbourhood pub in Clapham Old Town that has been here for over a hundred years. It was called The Tim Bobbin until 2010, when Tim went on sabbatical, and he’s now back above the door. Inside, the pub offers a Mediterranean seasonal menu with daily specials, including a Sunday roast rump of beef, plus a carefully selected international wine list and great tasting beer. The venue is described as having a cosy front room and an airy conservatory at the rear, with a wood-lined bar for more casual bar snacks.

name: The Windmill
description: The Windmill is an iconic pub on Clapham Common, a short stroll from Clapham Common and Clapham South tube stations. It’s known as a great spot to meet friends for a decent pint, with “flipping fantastic food” and a super dog-friendly welcome. The venue also offers 42 boutique-style bedrooms, including 13 dog-friendly rooms, with views over the Common. Food & drink highlights include epic breakfasts, long lunches, and slap-up suppers, plus Ginger Pig sharing dishes. The pub garden is promoted as Clapham’s best pub garden, and it hosts big-screen match-day events such as the Women’s Six Nations and the World Cup.

name: Two Brewers
description: Two Brewers Clapham is a legendary LGBTQIA+ venue at the heart of London’s gay scene, proudly serving the community since 1981. It’s known as a famous drag cabaret show bar and club, hosting glitter-filled cabaret extravaganzas seven nights a week. The venue also runs regular entertainment such as karaoke and quizzes, plus dancefloor nights until late. The page highlights “Front Row Pours” with limited-edition cocktails, and lists features including HD screens, late licence, live music, and a smoking area. It’s located at 114 Clapham High Street, Lambeth (SW4 7UJ).

name: VennStreet Records
description: Venn Street Records is a Clapham venue known as “the home of live music, cocktails & good times.” The page promotes regular DJ sets and live music sessions across the week, with named acts and set times. It also highlights a daily cocktail happy hour offering 2-4-1 cocktails from 5pm–8pm, and links to a drinks menu. The content includes booking prompts for events and encourages visitors to view all upcoming dates.

name: Courtfield
description: The Courtfield Earls Court is a traditional 19th-century pub with an ornate interior and a beer garden in Earl’s Court. It serves real ales and classic pub food in a family-friendly environment. The venue also promotes breakfast, Sunday roasts, private dining, and functions/venue hire. For sports fans, it highlights Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with events such as Six Nations (men’s and women’s) and live football, plus big-screen match viewing. Facilities listed include WiFi, disabled facilities, and it accepts coaches. Dogs are explicitly welcomed, and the pub is described as historic and family-friendly.

name: Earls Court Tavern
description: The Earls Court Tavern is a traditional corner pub in Earls Court, described as offering quality pub food, refreshing drinks and a vibrant West London atmosphere. It’s a short walk from Earls Court tube station and near the V&A. The venue promotes a menu of pub classics and small plates, plus a Sunday roast with classic trimmings. It also highlights sports viewing, including Sky Sports and TNT Sports, with events like Six Nations and live football. Facilities include disabled access, dog-friendly and family-friendly options, and WiFi. There are also booking options for tables and sports fixtures.

name: Prince Albert
description: The Prince Albert is a bright, cheerful British pub in Notting Hill, London, combining period features with contemporary touches and quirky charm. It sits at the heart of the neighbourhood and is home to the area’s famous indie Gate Theatre, with the intimate 75-seater theatre upstairs. Guests can relax in the welcoming bar, enjoy a glass of something special, and make the most of an inviting courtyard beer garden for lazy afternoons and al-fresco dining. The pub is also described as a great spot for laid-back lunches, family dinners, and social eats, with an explorative drinks menu and tempting, flavoursome food.

name: Sun in Splendour
description: The Sun in Splendour is a British pub in the heart of Notting Hill, London, offering a laid-back yet memorable drinking and dining experience. The venue is described as having individuality, character and quirky charm, with an “authentic, homely atmosphere” suitable for all occasions. The page highlights an explorative drinks menu and flavoursome food, and provides links to book a table, reserve online, and order from your seat. Opening hours are listed for every day, and the pub’s address is given on Portobello Road.

name: The Castle
description: The Castle Portobello is a British pub in the heart of London’s Portobello market, offering a laid-back yet memorable drinking and dining experience. It’s described as having individuality, character and quirky charm, with a homely atmosphere suitable for lazy lunches and family dinners. The page highlights an explorative drinks menu and “flavoursome food”, and provides links to book a table, order at table, and view the full menu. It also notes the pub is directly opposite the blue door featured in the film ‘Notting Hill’. Opening hours run daily, with later finishes on Fridays and Saturdays.

name: The Cock and Bottle
description: The Cock & Bottle is a traditional British pub in Notting Hill, on the corner of Needham Road and Artesian Road. It has a community feel and serves cask ales, fine wines and a range of spirits. Food is available seven days a week, including famous Sunday roasts, with British nostalgic classics such as fish and chips and sausage and mash, plus bar snacks, starters, mains and desserts. The pub also hosts parties and events, with private hire upstairs in the first-floor dining room (The Sutherland Room) and a private bar. Live sports are shown on multiple screens (TNT and Sky Sports), and there are regular pub quiz nights on Tuesdays. There’s also a sunny terrace for spritz season.

name: The Duke of Wellington
description: The Duke of Wellington is a traditional London pub in the heart of Notting Hill on Portobello Road, known for a friendly, welcoming atmosphere and a wide range of cask ales. It serves classic British food including fish & chips and Sunday roasts, with the kitchen open all day. The pub has outdoor seating and large windows overlooking Portobello Market for people-watching. It also has an outdoor space with tables outside, plus a first-floor private dining room with its own bar and toilet facilities. The venue is dog-friendly (dog bowls provided) and shows the FIFA World Cup 2026 live on big screens.

name: The Elgin
description: The Elgin is a dog-friendly pub in iconic Notting Hill, set between Ladbroke Grove and Holland Park and sitting at the top of Portobello Road. It’s described as a great spot for everything from post-work pints and relaxed family lunches to private parties, with multiple spaces for different occasions. The pub is proud of its food, with menus covering British seasonality including canapés, alfresco light lunches, Sunday roasts and dinners. There’s also a dedicated bar for cocktails and tipples, plus a beer garden. The venue highlights live sport with multiple screens and match-day meals.

name: The Ladbroke Arms
description: The Ladbroke Arms is a cosy neighbourhood pub in Notting Hill, described as a “Notting Hill’s Hidden Gem”. It offers a curated selection of drinks alongside seasonal dishes made with sustainable produce, and it’s noted for award-winning food—winning The Rosette Award for Culinary Excellence three years in a row. The pub serves Sunday roasts and promotes “Curated by chefs”. Facilities include being dog friendly, family friendly, and offering WiFi. It also provides booking and menu links, with serving hours shown throughout the week.

name: The Lock and Lantern
description: The Lock & Lantern is a historic Westbourne Park pub built around 1865, originally known as the Metropolitan pub. It’s named for the Metropolitan Railway and retains much of its Victorian character, including a prominent red granite surround. The pub serves great food and beer, with a focus on pizzas and a drinks line-up of British and Irish favourites on tap. It also hosts live boxing events and offers live sport with Sky Sports and TNT, creating a lively atmosphere. The venue can be hired for private functions for groups from 2 to 100 people.

name: The Mitre
description: The Mitre is a gastropub in Holland Park, described as a warm, welcoming place where exceptional food is served alongside an extensive selection of wines and ales. The page promotes a “Prix Fixe Menu” with two courses for £18 or three courses for £22, available 12–8pm Monday–Thursday. It also invites guests to join for dinner and drinks, and links to menus and booking. The pub positions itself as the “home of the action” for World Cup moments, with fixtures available to view.

name: The Stewart Arms
description: The Stewart Arms is a traditional local pub in Notting Hill, offering a wide variety of drinks and exciting offers. It’s open daily from 11:00 AM to 11:00 PM, with a welcoming atmosphere for relaxing with a pint. The venue also highlights facilities including a beer garden, dartboard, and live music, alongside sports viewing with TNT Sports and Sky Sports.

name: Walmer Castle
description: Walmer Castle is a revamped historic neighbourhood freehouse in Notting Hill, just yards from Portobello Road. Since 1845, it’s described as a Notting Hill landmark with spruce London pub décor, a quietly remarkable art collection, and an affable, welcoming team. The pub offers British-inspired dining with lunch and dinner served in the restaurant and bar, alongside a bar with extended opening hours. It also has thoughtfully designed spaces across three storeys, live music, and a smart private dining room (The Westbourne Room) for up to 20 guests.

name: Crown and Sceptre
description: The Crown & Sceptre is a traditional pub in the backstreets of Shepherds Bush, with an “enchanting and cosy secret garden” for a relaxed escape. It serves authentic Thai food, with dining from starters to pudding, alongside a well-stocked bar offering craft beer, cocktails and traditional drinks. The pub also highlights live sport, and mentions QPR home games with a pre-match atmosphere, opening at 10:30am and serving ales and draught products. Facilities include board games, free WiFi, baby changing facilities, families welcome, air conditioning, and assistance dogs welcome.

name: Pocket Watch
description: The Pocket Watch Pub – Shepherds Bush is a newly refurbished pub in Shepherds Bush, formerly the British Queen. It offers a great atmosphere to enjoy great drinks, freshly cooked stone baked pizzas, weekly Sunday roasts, and lovely weekend breakfasts. The pub is also described as a perfect place to watch live sporting events, with two large screen TVs, and it’s just minutes from Loftus Road Stadium—ideal for pre or post match drinks for QPR fans.

name: Princess Victoria
description: The Princess Victoria is a historic gin palace built in 1829, now an elegant public house with bedrooms. It features a handsome horseshoe bar serving over 100 artisan and big-name gins, real ales and an excellent wine list. There’s also a stunning dining room and a private party room, plus a new heated front terrace and rear courtyard garden. Food focuses on quality ingredients from small producers across the British Isles, including free-range Sunday roasts, responsibly sourced fish, and vegan and vegetarian dishes. The pub offers five individually designed boutique bedrooms with gin-cocktail-inspired themes and modern amenities.

name: The Askew
description: The Askew is a laid-back West London local pub in Shepherds Bush with a friendly, welcoming atmosphere. It’s known for a great pint and “proper pub food”, including Sunday roasts. The pub hosts regular events such as Friday bingo, Saturday live music, and Sunday karaoke. There’s also a garden that’s covered, heated and open all year round. The venue also shows live sport on big screens, making it a popular spot to catch the match.

name: The Bush Tavern
description: The Bush Tavern is a new neighbourhood pub and event space in the heart of Shepherds Bush. It offers freshly made cocktails, Bird House Brewery beer, and an eclectic wine list, alongside signature burgers and sides from No Drama. The venue is dog-friendly and mostly walk-in, with bookings available for groups of 8 or more. It also supports semi-private dining and full private hire. For major sport, it screens the World Cup on multiple screens, showing all group stages during opening hours. The page also highlights a lively events atmosphere with live music and DJ-style vibes.

name: The Central Bar
description: The Central Bar is located on the first floor of the W12 Shopping Centre, opposite the Central line tube station in Shepherd’s Bush. It’s open daily from 8:00am, with late closing times (up to 1:00am on Fridays and Saturdays). The pub offers Wi‑Fi and TV screens, and provides step-free access and a baby changing station. Food is available via the Wetherspoon app, including children’s meals priced at £4.99 and £5.75, served with a drink and fruit. The page also includes a short local transport history for the area.

name: The Defector's Weld
description: Defector's Weld is a lively pub in Shepherd’s Bush (170 Uxbridge Rd, London W12 8AA) known for its food and events. It serves food 12pm–10pm and offers a menu with fresh, British and seasonal ingredients, including items like Defector’s Chip Shop, BBQ wings, drunken peach wings, and smoked ox cheek doughnuts. The venue has an industrial-style, covered courtyard for outdoor pints and summer sessions, plus a private hire space upstairs (Philby’s) and options in the front/back bars for parties. The pub also hosts DJs, quizzes, karaoke and pop-ups, is dog-friendly, and shows major sports like the World Cup across screens.

name: The Eagle
description: The Eagle is a British pub offering seasonal, sustainable food and “delicious pub food”, with menus available online. It’s known as Ravenscourt’s favourite local, with a friendly team and a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere. A key highlight is its beautiful, leafy beer garden with plenty of seating, cosy huts for smaller gatherings, and a Burger Shack serving throughout the weekend. The pub also promotes events for all ages, including quiz nights and Father’s Day. For sports, it advertises Football World Cup viewing with relaxed meals or drinks in the garden before late kick-offs on screens. Dogs are welcome in the pub.

name: The Pavilion
description: The Pavilion in Shepherds Bush is a Greene King pub with a focus on live sport and a lively match-day atmosphere. It offers a “New Menu” and “Delicious Pub Food”, with weekly deals such as Lunch Club, Small Plates, Burger & a Drink, and Sunday Roasts. The venue also promotes watching major rugby and live football, and highlights Sky Sports and TNT Sports. There’s a beer garden for outdoor drinks, plus WiFi, car park, takeaway, and disabled facilities. The pub is explicitly dog friendly and is described as a historic pub, with facilities for functions and events.

name: The White Horse
description: White Horse Shepherds Bush is a traditional local pub in London (31 Uxbridge Road, Shepherd's Bush). It offers a wide variety of drinks with “unbeatable” drink offers. The pub is set up for live sport, with TNT Sports and Sky Sports, and it says it will be showing every match live for events such as the World Cup 2026. There’s also mention of Wi‑Fi and an “Outside Area”, suggesting outdoor space for guests. Opening times are listed daily, with today open 11:00 AM–10:00 PM.

name: Duke of Kent
description: The Duke of Kent is a historic pub in leafy Pitshanger, Ealing (Scotch Common, London W13 8DL). It’s known for “great fresh food, fine wines” and has the “best pub garden in Ealing”, with outdoor highlights including a bar, BBQ, private glasshouse and table-tennis tables. Inside, it offers a menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, plus a well-stocked bar featuring modern craft beers and cask classics. The pub also hosts events throughout the year and can cater for private events such as business meetings, weddings and birthdays.

name: The Drayton Court
description: The Drayton Court Hotel is a Fuller's venue in Ealing, set in one of London’s greenest suburbs. It offers 27 boutique rooms and a pub with an “amazing” beer garden described as the biggest in London. Dining includes light snacks, hearty mains and Sunday roasts, with food served daily. The venue also supports events such as weddings (two licensed spaces, receptions up to 200 guests), corporate meetings and private hire. There’s live sport with TNT Sports and a big screen for sports viewing, plus regular “What’s On” events including live music, DJs and pub quizzes.

name: The Forester
description: Built in 1909, The Forester is a Grade II listed pub in Ealing with charming original features across three bars, complemented by a recent refurbishment. It offers Thai-inspired dining with dishes cooked and served as they would be in Thailand, with set food serving times. The pub also hosts private events, from business meetings to weddings and birthdays. Live sport is shown on big screens, including Six Nations and Premier League/Champions League action. The venue is family-friendly and has a real fire, free WiFi, and assistance dogs welcome.

name: The Leather Saddle
description: The Leather Saddle is a pub venue in West Ealing, London, at 138 Broadway (W13 0TL). The page notes it was formerly Hennesseys Irish Bar. The listing includes venue details, a map section, and links to gigs and reviews, but shows “Gigs (0)” and “Reviews (0)”.

name: The Old Hat
description: The Old Hat is a friendly local pub in the heart of Ealing (West Ealing). It’s known for warm hospitality, “good times” and a lively weekend atmosphere, with live music that helps the pub come alive. The venue has a welcoming, history-filled feel, described as having walls that tell stories. Alongside drinks (including a perfect pint of Guinness), it offers delicious pub classics and food and drink specials, with a “new menu” mentioned in social content. The page also highlights regular events such as bingo on Wednesday nights and live music on Saturdays.

name: The Owl and the Pussycat
description: The Owl & The Pussycat is a micro-brew-pub, described as being “Twenty feet from Grain to Glass”. The page highlights a beer menu and provides 2022 opening hours (Mon–Sat 16:00–22:00, Sun 13:00–17:00). It also links to events and a beers section, and includes social links (Facebook and Untappd).

name: Crown & Sceptre
description: The Crown & Sceptre is renowned for its dynamic music, cracking food and drink, warm hospitality, good banter and events. Pub, Club, Kitchen, Outdoor seating terrace and Five Hotel Rooms. Opening hours: Midday to Midnight. Our Kitchen is due to open in around four weeks

name: Curtains Up
description: The Curtains Up is a historic West London pub in the heart of Barons Court, a short walk from Barons Court and West Kensington stations. It serves seasonal British food from brunch through to supper, alongside a wide selection of wines, ales, craft beers and spritz. The menu focuses on traditional pub classics and seasonal specials, with an emphasis on sustainability and championing British farmers and fisheries. The pub also hosts theatre: Barons Court Theatre is described as an intimate venue in the pub’s cellar vaults. There’s a welcoming, stylish-yet-cosy interior and the pub is dog-friendly.

name: The Albion
description: The Albion is a traditional English, independent and family-run pub in West London, just steps from the London Olympia exhibition centre. It has a cosy, countryside atmosphere and offers a carefully selected range of draft beers, wines and spirits. The pub is dog-friendly and focuses on good food and drink, serving homemade comfort dishes and freshly prepared stone-baked pizzas. Visitors can also view drink and food menus via the site. The venue offers group bookings for 20–40 people, a 1st floor private bar for up to 50, and whole pub hire for events up to 150.

name: The Bird in Hand
description: The Bird in Hand is a venue in Brook Green with unique decor that blends restaurant functionality and stylish furnishings. Evenings are described as a mix of business and pleasure, with options for a post-5pm rest bite or a glass before heading home. For dinner, it offers relaxed dining with small plates, big pizzas, and main courses. The page also highlights its pizza credentials, including flour from Molino Dallagiovanna and a slow proving process for a crispy, highly digestible pizza.

name: The Cumberland Arms
description: The Cumberland Arms is a cosy local pub just around the corner from Kensington Olympia, offering a great selection of beers and a well-chosen international wine list. It serves a Mediterranean-based menu inspired by carefully selected ingredients delivered daily from the markets, with food described as mixing seasonal British ingredients with Italian know-how. The site encourages visitors to come for a drink and a bite to eat, and provides links to view the menu, book a table, and find the pub. Reviews highlighted include a very enjoyable meal, a lovely atmosphere, and a cracking Med-inspired menu.

name: The Elm
description: The Elm is a friendly local London pub in the heart of Fulham, aiming to be a warm, welcoming hub for the community and a comfortable stop for tourists and passers-by. It offers a classic English pub feel with superb British ale, craft beer, and good quality wine and spirits, with a back-to-basics approach. The page also mentions “20 years plus of experience” and a team focused on good beer, good conversation, and good times. The venue is available for private hire to plan events.

name: The Hand and Flower
description: The Hand & Flower is a beautiful Victorian pub & hotel in the heart of Hammersmith, just down the road from Earl’s Court and Olympia London. It has 10 luxurious guest rooms in a historic, century-old building, including a stay option opposite Olympia London. The pub offers a seasonal menu of refined pub classics made with fresh, seasonal ingredients, alongside an extensive drinks range with modern craft beers and cask classics. It also highlights live sport shown with TNT Sports on a big screen, plus facilities such as step-free access and assistance dogs welcome. The venue can cater for private events including business meetings, weddings, and birthdays.

name: The Havelock Tavern
description: The Havelock Tavern in Brook Green is a laid-back gastropub known as one of London’s original gastropubs. It offers a relaxed, lively atmosphere with seasonal dishes, including a Prix Fixe menu (two courses £18 or three courses £22, 12–8pm Monday–Thursday) and a Spring–Summer menu launching 19 March. The pub also runs weekly offers such as Wing Wednesday and £25 Prosecco bottles every Friday. Facilities include WiFi, and it’s described as dog- and family-friendly. There’s also an outdoor beer garden for al fresco dining, with a covered area and heaters.

name: The Warwick Arms
description: The Warwick Arms in Kensington is a traditional-style pub tucked between Olympia and Earl’s Court. It’s known for hearty ales, including fresh cask ales, and friendly, old-fashioned service. At mealtimes it offers home-cooked North Indian cuisine (“Indian Dream”), alongside British pub classics like fish & chips and homemade pies, plus lighter lunch options such as wraps and smaller portions. The pub features include food served, outside seating, a real fire, and paid parking nearby. It also welcomes children aged 8 and over, and provides menu links and food times for dining.

name: Ticket Hall
description: Cahoots Ticket Hall is an all-new 1940s black market pub on Soho’s Kingly Street. It’s open every day from noon until late, with a laid-back, classic 1940s British pub atmosphere. The Scoundrels serve draught beers, pale ales, cocktails, wines and spirits. There’s a spacious outdoor drinking area on Kingly Street (walk-ins only for the outdoor terrace). Lunch is available with a lunchtime menu of classic British pub dishes such as beer-battered cod, bangers & mash and lunchtime sarnies, with bookings 12pm–3.45pm and last orders for lunch at 4.30pm. The venue also offers private party hire with vintage posters, high-level seating and a giant station clock.

name: The Blue Posts
description: The Blue Posts is a historic pub in Soho, described as part of Soho’s fabric since the 1720s. It’s close to Carnaby Street and Regent Street, with a traditional pub feel and a “new look” interior that pays homage to its history. The venue offers a bountiful bar with well-kept cask ales, craft beers, wines, cocktails, and hot drinks. Food is available with a menu covering pub snacks, sharers, starters, sandwiches, mains and puddings, plus lunch options and a Sunday roast theme. Facilities include a beer garden, WiFi, and functions, and the pub is dog friendly.

name: The Clachan
description: The Clachan is a historic pub in Soho, described as being in the heart of London on Kingly Street, just off Regent Street. The page highlights a focus on “perfect pints” and “unbeatable pies”, with British pub classic menus and tempting dishes. It also mentions options to book a table, order at the table, and order for collection. The venue is positioned near central London attractions, including Oxford Circus Underground Station (a three-minute walk).

name: The Glassblower
description: The Glass Blower Piccadilly is a family-friendly, dog-friendly pub in Soho, originally a red brick pub. It’s less than five minutes from Piccadilly Circus tube station and close to shops. The venue offers a menu of pub food including small plates and hearty pub classics, with highlights such as Sunday Roast. There are facilities including WiFi, takeaway, and offers functions. The page also mentions booking tables and functions, plus “big screens at the ready” for major events like the World Cup.

name: The Leicester Arms
description: The Leicester Arms Piccadilly is a historic corner pub in Piccadilly, first licensed in 1725. It’s described as a relaxing place to “relax and revive,” with a family-friendly welcome and a dog-friendly policy. Food is a key part of the offer, including a seasonal specials menu, “Delicious Pub Food,” and a Sunday Roast with classic trimmings. The pub is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, and it promotes live football and Six Nations rugby screenings. Facilities mentioned include WiFi, disabled facilities, takeaway, and function rooms for meetings, birthdays and events.

name: The Wigmore
description: The Wigmore is a modern British tavern with a luxury twist, set in a former banking hall. Inspired by classic British public houses, it offers a warm, social space for drinking, dining and gathering, with a menu overseen by Michel Roux featuring hearty British dishes reimagined with a refined touch. The venue serves wines on tap, house punches, ‘hoptails’, cask ales and craft beers, plus a signature brew called “Saison”. Located on Regent Street in London’s West End, it’s suitable for everything from lunch to lively evenings. There are also multiple event spaces, including an outdoor terrace (“The Hatch”).

name: City Of Quebec
description: The City of Quebec Marylebone is an Art Deco LGBTQIA+ pub and a long-standing cornerstone of London’s gay community since 1946. It’s known for a vibrant venue with a stage for cabaret and live events, including drag performances. The pub offers food alongside drinks, with menus and dish highlights such as small plates and pizzas. There’s also a beer garden for outdoor drinks (weather permitting). Facilities mentioned include disabled facilities, WiFi, and offers/functions, plus it’s dog friendly.

name: Spread Eagle
description: The Spread Eagle Mayfair is a pub in Mayfair where you can take a moment away from the city. It originally stood on Oxford Street from the 17th century, then was rebuilt set back in 1955. The venue offers space to sit outside and watch the world go by, and it’s known for food at the heart of the experience, including pub classics and a traditional Sunday roast. It also has facilities for functions and is set up for sports viewing, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, plus live match screenings such as rugby and live football. Dog-friendly and family-friendly, with WiFi and offers.

name: Admiral Duncan
description: Admiral Duncan London is a friendly pub with a “Local” atmosphere in the heart of the capital, on Old Compton Street. The venue is known for an eclectic mix of customers and a vibrant bar, and it hosts a range of event nights. The page highlights live entertainment such as Sunday Night Cabaret, Monday Night Karaoke, and weekly cabaret acts (with dates and times listed). It also notes features including Wi‑Fi and an outside area, and states it is an over-18s venue where ID may be requested on entry or at the bar.

name: Comptons of Soho
description: Comptons London is a celebrated LGBTQIA+ venue on Old Compton Street, built on the site of the 200-year-old Swiss Hotel. It has been at the centre of the gay scene since 1986 and is described as a welcoming “Grande Dame” and a steadfast heart of gay Soho. The page highlights seasonal cocktails (“Front Row Pours”) and a busy programme of events, including DJ nights and themed socials. The venue also notes it is cask marque approved and offers real ale, with Wi‑Fi and a smoking area.

name: De Hems
description: De Hems Dutch Cafe Bar is an authentic Dutch pub tucked away down a Soho side street, on the corner of Chinatown. It’s described as London’s one and only authentic Dutch pub, with deep history and tradition—formerly a watering hole for Dutch sailors and an unofficial HQ of the Dutch World War II resistance. The venue offers a laid-back, homely atmosphere with flavoursome food, an explorative drinks menu, and options for a lazy lunch or a family dinner. Table booking and table ordering are available online, and the page also links to food and events sections.

name: Duke of Wellington
description: Duke Of Wellington London is a pub in Westminster at 77 Wardour Street, open from midday until late. The venue promotes “Front Row Pours” with limited-edition cocktail features and highlights its bar atmosphere. It also runs a busy events programme including DJ nights, bingo, and pub quiz. Facilities listed include real ale (Cask Marque Approved), HD screens, Wi‑Fi, accessible toilets, wheelchair access, and an outside area. The page also notes it is a dog-friendly pub and includes live entertainment.

name: French House
description: The French House is an iconic Soho pub known for a warm welcome and a lively mix of actors, writers, artists and film-world regulars. It offers a choice of thirty champagnes and wines by the glass, and is described as a haven for conversation thanks to its “no music, no machines, no television and no mobile phones” rule. The bar is open Monday to Friday 11:30–11pm and Sundays 12pm–10:30pm, with drinks served on a first-come, first-served basis. An upstairs restaurant is available for lunch (midday–3pm) and dinner (6pm–9:30pm) with daily-changing menus and limited seating.

name: Golden Lion
description: The Golden Lion Soho is a traditional yet modern Greene King pub just off Shaftesbury Avenue in London’s West End Theatre area. It’s a great spot to stop in after a show, with a welcoming atmosphere and a menu of pub classics and small plates, including Sunday roasts. The venue is set up for sports fans, with Sky Sports and TNT Sports, plus big-screen viewing for live football and rugby events like the Six Nations, and it also promotes live fixtures and match-day bookings. Facilities include WiFi and the Greene King Sport App, and it’s listed as dog and family friendly. There’s also mention of functions and a function room for celebrations.

name: Royal George
description: The Royal George is a pub in Charing Cross, London, described as one of Soho’s hidden gems with “dazzling interiors” and “quirky décor”. It offers classic pub food, craft beers and an “authentic, homely atmosphere”. The venue is positioned for catch-ups and get-togethers, and it also hosts open mic nights. It’s set near major landmarks including Leicester Square, The National Gallery, The British Museum and the River Thames, making it a convenient stop for a laid-back drinking and dining experience.

name: Rupert Street
description: Rupert Street Bar London is a chic LGBTQIA+ bar in Soho, with a gorgeous interior for celebrations and cocktails. The venue is known for legendary weekend vibes, hosted by queer DJs and performers, and it offers a cocktail menu including limited-edition seasonal drinks. The page also lists upcoming drag cabaret and DJ events. Facilities mentioned include HD screens, a cocktail menu, live music, an outside area, smoking area, beer garden, and dog-friendly policy, alongside accessibility features like wheelchair access and accessible toilets.

name: The Coach & Horses
description: The Coach & Horses is one of Soho’s oldest pubs, dating back to 1731. Set in the heart of London’s Theatreland on the corner of Old Compton Street and Charing Cross Road, it’s a cosy, characterful spot for pre-theatre drinks or a break while exploring. The pub offers a wide selection of cask ales and lagers, plus a carefully selected wine list and traditional spirits. It also highlights its historic Grade II listed building and notes that Shepherd Neame restored the original name as part of a major refurbishment. The venue is open every day and available to hire for events throughout the year.

name: The Coach and Horses
description: The Coach & Horses, Soho is a historic London pub with a well-stocked bar offering modern craft beers and cask classics. It’s described as a deeply loved London institution with rich history, and it’s voted Evening Standard’s number 1 pub to visit in London. The venue welcomes families and assistance dogs, offers free WiFi, and has outside seating. It also states “Dog Friendly” and provides step-free access. The page notes limited capacity and that the pub does not take table bookings, welcoming walk-ins instead.

name: The Crown & Two Chairmen
description: The Crown & Two Chairmen in London combines British pub hospitality with “individuality, character and quirky charm”. It’s positioned as a laid-back yet memorable place for drinking and dining, with an explorative drinks menu and “tempting and flavoursome food”. The page also highlights ways to book a table online, order from your seat, and buy gift cards. Opening hours are listed for every day, and the venue is located at 31–32 Dean Street, London (W1D 3SB).

name: The Dog and Duck
description: The Dog and Duck is a historic, Grade II listed pub in Soho with a rich story dating back to 1734, and a present building built in 1897 by architect Francis Cannon. The pub is known for its exquisite period interior, including thousands of glazed tiles, mahogany panelling, and decorative mirrors. It’s also associated with famous visitors such as George Orwell, John Constable, Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and Madonna. The pub offers British pub classics with “perfect pints and unbeatable pies”, with food available via its menus and the option to order at table or book a table. Opening hours run from midday through the evening.

name: The Flying Horse
description: Welcome to Flying Horse, a historic pub in Tottenham Court Road (Oxford Street, London). The page describes it as a traditional pub with unique character, known for an eclectic range of real ales served with a generous measure of British hospitality. It also promotes British pub classic menus with “unbeatable pies” and tempting dishes, and offers options to book a table, order at table, and buy gift cards. The venue is positioned as being within a short stroll of Tottenham Court Road, Charing Cross Road and New Oxford Street.

name: The Lyric
description: The Lyric is Soho’s local, described as the area’s oldest independent free house near Piccadilly Circus. It offers craft beer, real cask ales, fine wines, and pub classics including fish and chips and Sunday roasts, with a warm, friendly welcome. The pub is set in a cosy ambience and invites visitors to relax while catching live sports.

name: The Montagu Pyke
description: The Montagu Pyke is a Wetherspoon pub on Charing Cross Road (also at 20 Greek Street) in Westminster. The building’s main frontage was originally Pyke’s Cambridge Circus Cinematograph Theatre, built in 1911; after a fire in 1915 it was restored as the Super cinema, later becoming the Tatler, Filmcenta and the three-screen Cannon. In 1988 it became the Marquee Club, closing in 1996. Today it offers TV screens and step-free access, with music mentioned in the facilities list. Opening hours run from 12:00pm to 11:00pm on most days (Sunday closes at 10:00pm), with serving hours until 9:00pm (Sunday until 8:00pm). Facilities include WiFi, and it’s described as dog-friendly and family-friendly. The pub also offers functions and venue hire, including packages for business events, parties and weddings, plus a private dining room upstairs.

name: The Porterhouse
description: Porterhouse in Covent Garden is a large, family-owned pub split over three main floors with three bars and mezzanine levels. It serves craft beer and “quality pub grub”, with a menu including fish & chips, burgers, pizzas and homemade Sunday roasts, plus vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options. The venue also has one of Central London’s largest beer gardens and a Terrace. Sports fans can watch major sporting events (especially rugby) on 18 screens. Live music is held in the Basement Bar every Thursday, Friday and Saturday with house bands playing rock and pop covers.

name: The Wellington
description: The Wellington is an historic pub on The Strand, dating back to 1903. It’s known for its stunning neo-gothic interiors, including a sculpted ground-floor ceiling, stained glass windows, and a large, cosy original marble fireplace. The pub is presented as a place for “perfect pints” and British pub classic menus, with tempting dishes and options to book a table or order at the table/for collection.
